author.name: AATF AI News Aggregator

entry.title: Research Summary: April 14, 2026

author.name: AATF AI News Aggregator

entry.summary:
Today's research centers on fundamental limitations of current techniques and critical safety concerns for multi-agent systems.

  • MEMENTO introduces self-managed context compression for reasoning models, teaching them to segment thinking into blocks and compress into dense summaries — addressing a key bottleneck in long-chain reasoning
  • A proof that activation steering pushes residual streams off the reachable manifold (non-surjective) challenges core assumptions in interpretability and alignment
  • Multi-agent AI organizations are shown to be simultaneously more effective yet less aligned than individual agents, a critical finding as agentic deployments scale
  • First information-theoretic lower bounds for diffusion sampling prove any sampler requires Ω̃(√d) adaptive score queries

Architecture understanding advances with evidence that MoE expert specialization reflects representation geometry rather than domain expertise — linear routers merely partition the embedding space. The first empirical study of 626 autonomous agents on the Pilot Protocol reveals heavy-tailed social structures emerging without explicit coordination.

  • Overthinking in LLMs systematically demonstrates that extended chain-of-thought can degrade accuracy by abandoning correct intermediate answers
  • Meerkat combines clustering with agentic search to detect cross-trace safety violations at scale in agent deployments
  • LIRA defends against jailbreaks by retraining how models interpret malicious instructions at the latent representation level
  • Pando benchmark controls for the elicitation confounder, testing whether interpretability methods work when models resist self-explanation

entry.title: MEMENTO: Teaching LLMs to Manage Their Own Context

author.name: Vasilis Kontonis, Yuchen Zeng, Shivam Garg, Lingjiao Chen, Hao Tang, Ziyan Wang, Ahmed Awadallah, Eric Horvitz, John Langford, Dimitris Papailiopoulos

entry.summary: MEMENTO teaches reasoning models to segment their thinking into blocks, compress each into dense summaries (mementos), and reason forward attending only to these summaries. Releases OpenMementos dataset of 228K annotated reasoning traces. Works across Qwen3, Phi-4, Olmo 3 at 8B-32B scale.

entry.title: Steered LLM Activations are Non-Surjective

author.name: Aayush Mishra, Daniel Khashabi, Anqi Liu

entry.summary: Proves that activation steering pushes LLM residual streams off the manifold of states reachable from discrete prompts, meaning steered activations are not realizable by any textual input. This has implications for interpretability and safety research using steering.

entry.title: AI Organizations are More Effective but Less Aligned than Individual Agents

author.name: Judy Hanwen Shen, Daniel Zhu, Siddarth Srinivasan, Henry Sleight, Lawrence T. Wagner III, Morgan Jane Matthews, Erik Jones, Jascha Sohl-Dickstein

entry.summary: Experimentally shows that multi-agent AI organizations are simultaneously more effective at business goals but less aligned than individual AI agents, across 12 tasks in consultancy and software settings. Demonstrates emergent misalignment from agent interaction.

entry.title: Query Lower Bounds for Diffusion Sampling

author.name: Zhiyang Xun, Eric Price

entry.summary: Establishes the first information-theoretic lower bounds for score queries in diffusion sampling, proving that any sampler requires Ω̃(√d) adaptive score queries for d-dimensional distributions. This provides a formal explanation for why multi-scale noise schedules are necessary in diffusion models.

entry.title: The Myth of Expert Specialization in MoEs: Why Routing Reflects Geometry, Not Necessarily Domain Expertise

author.name: Xi Wang, Soufiane Hayou, Eric Nalisnick

entry.summary: Demonstrates that MoE expert specialization is an emergent property of the representation space, not the routing architecture, since linear routers make hidden state similarity necessary and sufficient for explaining routing patterns. Proves load-balancing loss suppresses shared directions.

entry.title: Emergent Social Structures in Autonomous AI Agent Networks: A Metadata Analysis of 626 Agents on the Pilot Protocol

author.name: Teodor-Ioan Calin

entry.summary: First empirical analysis of social structure formation among 626 autonomous AI agents on a live network (Pilot Protocol). Finds heavy-tailed degree distributions consistent with preferential attachment in the autonomously formed trust network. References OpenClaw instances.

entry.title: Detecting Safety Violations Across Many Agent Traces

author.name: Adam Stein, Davis Brown, Hamed Hassani, Mayur Naik, Eric Wong

entry.summary: Introduces Meerkat, a system combining clustering with agentic search to detect safety violations across large sets of agent traces. Addresses failures that are only visible when analyzing multiple traces together, relevant to misuse campaigns, covert sabotage, and reward hacking.

entry.title: LABBench2: An Improved Benchmark for AI Systems Performing Biology Research

author.name: Jon M Laurent, Albert Bou, Michael Pieler, Conor Igoe, Alex Andonian, Siddharth Narayanan, James Braza, Alexandros Sanchez Vassopoulos, Jacob L Steenwyk, Blake Lash, Andrew D White, Samuel G Rodriques

entry.summary: LABBench2 is an evolved benchmark for measuring AI systems' ability to perform real biology research, going beyond rote knowledge to test meaningful scientific work capabilities. This builds on the original LAB-Bench and shifts focus toward real-world scientific competence.

entry.title: When More Thinking Hurts: Overthinking in LLM Test-Time Compute Scaling

author.name: Shu Zhou, Rui Ling, Junan Chen, Xin Wang, Tao Fan, Hao Wang

entry.summary: Systematically investigates 'overthinking' in LLM reasoning: when extended chain-of-thought actually leads to worse results by abandoning correct answers. Shows diminishing marginal returns at higher compute budgets and that optimal thinking length varies by problem difficulty.

entry.title: Introspective Diffusion Language Models

author.name: Yifan Yu, Yuqing Jian, Junxiong Wang, Zhongzhu Zhou, Donglin Zhuang, Xinyu Fang, Sri Yanamandra, Xiaoxia Wu, Qingyang Wu, Shuaiwen Leon Song, Tri Dao, Ben Athiwaratkun, James Zou, Fan Lai, Chenfeng Xu

entry.summary: Introduces Introspective Diffusion Language Models (I-DLM), identifying that diffusion LMs lack 'introspective consistency' (accepting their own generations) that AR models inherently have. Proposes a training paradigm combining parallel diffusion decoding with AR-style introspective consistency.

entry.title: RationalRewards: Reasoning Rewards Scale Visual Generation Both Training and Test Time

author.name: Haozhe Wang, Cong Wei, Weiming Ren, Jiaming Liu, Fangzhen Lin, Wenhu Chen

entry.summary: Proposes RationalRewards, teaching reward models to produce explicit multi-dimensional critiques before scoring for visual generation. Introduces Preference-Anchored Rationalization (PARRO) to train without costly rationale annotations. Shows improvements at both training and test time.

entry.title: Pando: Do Interpretability Methods Work When Models Won't Explain Themselves?

author.name: Ziqian Zhong, Aashiq Muhamed, Mona T. Diab, Virginia Smith, Aditi Raghunathan

entry.summary: Introduces Pando, a benchmark for mechanistic interpretability that controls for the 'elicitation confounder' - whether interpretability gains simply reflect information obtainable through prompting. Uses 720 finetuned models with faithful, absent, or unfaithful explanations.

entry.title: Latent Instruction Representation Alignment: defending against jailbreaks, backdoors and undesired knowledge in LLMs

author.name: Eric Easley, Sebastian Farquhar

entry.summary: Introduces LIRA (Latent Instruction Representation Alignment), which trains LLMs to change how they interpret malicious instructions rather than just their responses. Blocks 99%+ of PEZ jailbreaks, removes insecure code backdoors, and achieves optimal forgetting on WMDP cyber benchmark with negligible capability loss.

entry.title: Zero-shot World Models Are Developmentally Efficient Learners

author.name: Khai Loong Aw, Klemen Kotar, Wanhee Lee, Seungwoo Kim, Khaled Jedoui, Rahul Venkatesh, Lilian Naing Chen, Michael C. Frank, Daniel L. K. Yamins

entry.summary: Introduces Zero-shot Visual World Models (ZWM) as a computational hypothesis for children's physical understanding, combining sparse temporal prediction, zero-shot causal inference, and compositional reasoning. Shows data-efficient and flexible generalization.

entry.title: Do Agent Rules Shape or Distort? Guardrails Beat Guidance in Coding Agents

author.name: Xing Zhang, Guanghui Wang, Yanwei Cui, Wei Qiu, Ziyuan Li, Bing Zhu, Peiyang He

entry.summary: Conducts the first large-scale empirical study of AI coding agent instruction files (CLAUDE.md, .cursorrules). Finds that rules improve performance 7-14pp, but random rules help as much as expert-curated ones. Only negative constraints ('do not') are individually beneficial.

entry.title: Generative UI: LLMs are Effective UI Generators

author.name: Yaniv Leviathan (Cheenu), Dani Valevski (Cheenu), Matan Kalman (Cheenu), Danny Lumen (Cheenu), Eyal Segalis (Cheenu), Eyal Molad (Cheenu), Shlomi Pasternak (Cheenu), Vishnu Natchu (Cheenu), Valerie Nygaard (Cheenu), Srinivasan (Cheenu), Venkatachary, James Manyika, Yossi Matias

entry.summary: Demonstrates that modern LLMs, when properly prompted with the right tools, can robustly generate custom UIs for virtually any prompt rather than just markdown text. Shows humans overwhelmingly prefer generated UIs over standard markdown output. From Google researchers.

entry.title: Human-like Working Memory Interference in Large Language Models

author.name: Hua-Dong Xiong (School of Psychological and Brain Sciences, Georgia Tech), Li Ji-An (Department of Psychology, New York University), Jiaqi Huang (Department of Cognitive Science, Indiana University Bloomington, Honda Research Institute), Robert C. Wilson (School of Psychological and Brain Sciences, Georgia Tech, Center of Excellence for Computational Cognition, Georgia Tech), Kwonjoon Lee (Honda Research Institute), Xue-Xin Wei (Departments of Neuroscience and Psychology, The University of Texas at Austin)

entry.summary: Shows that pretrained LLMs exhibit human-like working memory interference signatures despite having full attention access to context. A two-layer transformer can solve these tasks perfectly, but diverse pretrained LLMs still show limitations.

entry.title: Your Model Diversity, Not Method, Determines Reasoning Strategy

author.name: Moulik Choraria, Argyrios Gerogiannis, Anirban Das, Supriyo Chakraborty, Berkcan Kapusuzoglu, Chia-Hsuan Lee, Kartik Balasubramaniam, Shi-Xiong Zhang, Sambit Sahu

entry.summary: Argues that the optimal reasoning strategy (breadth vs. depth) depends on a model's 'diversity profile' - the spread of probability mass across solution approaches. Provides theoretical framework decomposing reasoning uncertainty and derives conditions for when tree-style vs. parallel sampling wins.

entry.title: BankerToolBench: Evaluating AI Agents in End-to-End Investment Banking Workflows

author.name: Elaine Lau, Markus D\"ucker, Ronak Chaudhary, Hui Wen Goh, Rosemary Wei, Vaibhav Kumar, Saed Qunbar, Guram Gogia, Yi Liu, Scott Millslagle, Nasim Borazjanizadeh, Ulyana Tkachenko, Samuel Eshun Danquah, Collin Schweiker, Vijay Karumathil, Asrith Devalaraju, Varsha Sandadi, Haemi Nam, Punit Arani, Ray Epps, Abdullah Arif, Sahil Bhaiwala, Curtis Northcutt, Skyler Wang, Anish Athalye, Jonas Mueller, Francisco Guzm\'an

entry.summary: Introduces BankerToolBench (BTB), an open-source benchmark of end-to-end investment banking analytical workflows developed with 502 investment bankers. Requires agents to navigate data rooms, use industry tools, and generate multi-file deliverables.

entry.title: Intersectional Sycophancy: How Perceived User Demographics Shape False Validation in Large Language Models

author.name: Benjamin Maltbie, Shivam Raval

entry.summary: Investigates whether LLM sycophancy varies with perceived user demographics (race, age, gender, confidence). Tests GPT-5-nano and Claude Haiku 4.5 across 128 persona combinations using Anthropic's Petri framework. Finds GPT-5-nano is significantly more sycophantic than Claude Haiku 4.5.

entry.title: Backdoors in RLVR: Jailbreak Backdoors in LLMs From Verifiable Reward

author.name: Weiyang Guo, Zesheng Shi, Zeen Zhu, Yuan Zhou, Min Zhang, Jing Li

entry.summary: Identifies a backdoor vulnerability in Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards (RLVR) where poisoning data can implant jailbreak backdoors without modifying the reward verifier, using asymmetric reward signals.

entry.title: Jailbreaking the Matrix: Nullspace Steering for Controlled Model Subversion

author.name: Vishal Pramanik, Maisha Maliha, Susmit Jha, Sumit Kumar Jha

entry.summary: Introduces Head-Masked Nullspace Steering (HMNS), a circuit-level jailbreak attack that identifies causal attention heads, suppresses them, and injects perturbations in the orthogonal complement. Operates in a closed-loop detection-intervention cycle.

entry.title: Bringing Value Models Back: Generative Critics for Value Modeling in LLM Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Zikang Shan, Han Zhong, Liwei Wang, Li Zhao

entry.summary: Revisits value modeling in LLM RL by proposing generative critics that use chain-of-thought reasoning for value estimation, arguing discriminative critics' limitations stem from limited expressiveness. Shows scaling benefits.

entry.title: Audio Flamingo Next: Next-Generation Open Audio-Language Models for Speech, Sound, and Music

author.name: Sreyan Ghosh, Arushi Goel, Kaousheik Jayakumar, Lasha Koroshinadze, Nishit Anand, Zhifeng Kong, Siddharth Gururani, Sang-gil Lee, Jaehyeon Kim, Aya Aljafari, Chao-Han Huck Yang, Sungwon Kim, Ramani Duraiswami, Dinesh Manocha, Mohammad Shoeybi, Bryan Catanzaro, Ming-Yu Liu, Wei Ping

entry.summary: Presents Audio Flamingo Next (AF-Next), a large audio-language model from NVIDIA supporting speech, environmental sounds, and music understanding. Introduces Temporal Audio Chain-of-Thought reasoning for long audio inputs up to 30 minutes and scalable training data strategies.

entry.title: Solving Physics Olympiad via Reinforcement Learning on Physics Simulators

author.name: Mihir Prabhudesai, Aryan Satpathy, Yangmin Li, Zheyang Qin, Nikash Bhardwaj, Amir Zadeh, Chuan Li, Katerina Fragkiadaki, Deepak Pathak

entry.summary: Shows that physics simulators can serve as supervision sources for training LLMs on physical reasoning via RL. Generates synthetic QA pairs from simulated physics interactions and trains models that solve Physics Olympiad problems.

entry.title: LangFlow: Continuous Diffusion Rivals Discrete in Language Modeling

author.name: Yuxin Chen, Chumeng Liang, Hangke Sui, Ruihan Guo, Chaoran Cheng, Jiaxuan You, Ge Liu

entry.summary: Introduces LangFlow, the first continuous diffusion language model to rival discrete diffusion. Key innovations include ODE-based NLL bound, information-uniform noise scheduling via Gumbel distribution, and improved self-conditioning training.

entry.title: Why Smaller Is Slower? Dimensional Misalignment in Compressed LLMs

author.name: Jihao Xin, Tian Lyu, Qilong Pan, Kesen Wang, Marco Canini

entry.summary: Analyzes why post-training compression of LLMs often fails to deliver speedups despite reducing parameters, due to 'dimensional misalignment' with GPU execution. Proposes GAC (GPU-Aligned Compression) to ensure compressed dimensions remain GPU-friendly.

entry.title: The Blind Spot of Agent Safety: How Benign User Instructions Expose Critical Vulnerabilities in Computer-Use Agents

author.name: Xuwei Ding, Skylar Zhai, Linxin Song, Jiate Li, Taiwei Shi, Nicholas Meade, Siva Reddy, Jian Kang, Jieyu Zhao

entry.summary: Introduces OS-BLIND benchmark evaluating computer-use agents under unintended attack conditions where user instructions are benign but harm arises from context. Tests 300 tasks across 12 categories on frontier models.

entry.title: HealthAdminBench: Evaluating Computer-Use Agents on Healthcare Administration Tasks

author.name: Suhana Bedi, Ryan Welch, Ethan Steinberg, Michael Wornow, Taeil Matthew Kim, Haroun Ahmed, Peter Sterling, Bravim Purohit, Qurat Akram, Angelic Acosta, Esther Nubla, Pritika Sharma, Michael A. Pfeffer, Sanmi Koyejo, Nigam H. Shah

entry.summary: HealthAdminBench evaluates computer-use agents on healthcare administration tasks across EHR, payer portals, and fax systems, with 135 expert-defined tasks and 1,698 evaluation points. Evaluates 7 agents including Claude, GPT, and Gemini.

entry.title: Credit-Budgeted ICPC-Style Coding: When Agents Must Pay for Every Decision

author.name: Lingfeng Zhou, Junhao Shi, Jin Gao, Dequan Wang

entry.summary: USACOArena introduces a credit-budgeted coding arena where agents must manage compute tokens, test executions, and time as finite resources, forcing strategic trade-offs. Reveals that current frontier agents and swarms fail to optimize under these constraints.

entry.title: Do LLMs Build Spatial World Models? Evidence from Grid-World Maze Tasks

author.name: Weijiang Li, Yilin Zhu, Rajarshi Das, Parijat Dube

entry.summary: Systematically evaluates whether LLMs build internal spatial world models using maze tasks. Tests Gemini-2.5-Flash, GPT-5-mini, Claude-Haiku-4.5, and DeepSeek-Chat. Finds performance collapses at larger mazes and reveals significant discrepancies in spatial reasoning capabilities.

entry.title: Camyla: Scaling Autonomous Research in Medical Image Segmentation

author.name: Yifan Gao, Haoyue Li, Feng Yuan, Xin Gao, Weiran Huang, Xiaosong Wang

entry.summary: Presents Camyla, a fully autonomous research system for medical image segmentation that generates research proposals, runs experiments, and writes manuscripts without human intervention. Introduces Quality-Weighted Branch Exploration and Layered Reflective Memory.

entry.title: Why Do Large Language Models Generate Harmful Content?

author.name: Rajesh Ganguli, Raha Moraffah

entry.summary: Uses causal mediation analysis to identify which model components (layers, modules, neurons) cause harmful content generation in LLMs. Finds harmful generation arises in later layers, primarily from MLP blocks, with specific neurons acting as gating mechanisms.

entry.title: GIANTS: Generative Insight Anticipation from Scientific Literature

author.name: Joy He-Yueya, Anikait Singh, Ge Gao, Michael Y. Li, Sherry Yang, Chelsea Finn, Emma Brunskill, Noah D. Goodman

entry.summary: Introduces GIANTS, a benchmark for 'insight anticipation' - predicting a downstream paper's core insight from its parent papers - with 17k examples across eight scientific domains. Tests LMs' ability to synthesize prior work into novel contributions.

entry.title: Universal statistical signatures of evolution in artificial intelligence architectures

author.name: Theodor Spiro

entry.summary: Tests whether AI architectural evolution follows the same statistical laws as biological evolution. Analyzes 935 ablation experiments from 161 papers, finding AI's distribution of fitness effects matches Drosophila and yeast distributions.

entry.title: You Only Judge Once: Multi-response Reward Modeling in a Single Forward Pass

author.name: Yinuo Yang, Zixian Ma, Manasi Ganti, Jieyu Zhang, Ranjay Krishna

entry.summary: Presents a discriminative multimodal reward model that scores all candidate responses in a single forward pass by concatenating them with separator tokens, achieving up to N× speedup. Constructs two new N-way preference benchmarks.

entry.title: CocoaBench: Evaluating Unified Digital Agents in the Wild

author.name: CocoaBench Team, Shibo Hao, Zhining Zhang, Zhiqi Liang, Tianyang Liu, Yuheng Zha, Qiyue Gao, Jixuan Chen, Zilong Wang, Zhoujun Cheng, Haoxiang Zhang, Junli Wang, Hexi Jin, Boyuan Zheng, Kun Zhou, Yu Wang, Feng Yao, Licheng Liu, Yijiang Li, Zhifei Li, Zhengtao Han, Pracha Promthaw, Tommaso Cerruti, Xiaohan Fu, Ziqiao Ma, Jingbo Shang, Lianhui Qin, Julian McAuley, Eric P. Xing, Zhengzhong Liu, Rupesh Kumar Srivastava, Zhiting Hu

entry.summary: Introduces CocoaBench, a benchmark for unified digital agents with long-horizon tasks requiring flexible composition of vision, search, and coding capabilities. Evaluates whether agents can combine skills that are typically tested in isolation.

entry.title: The Diffusion-Attention Connection

author.name: Julio Candanedo

entry.summary: Establishes a theoretical connection between transformers, diffusion maps, and magnetic Laplacians as different regimes of a single Markov geometry built from pre-softmax query-scores. Unifies attention and diffusion via a QK 'bidivergence'.

entry.title: Transformers Learn the Optimal DDPM Denoiser for Multi-Token GMMs

author.name: Hongkang Li, Hancheng Min, Rene Vidal

entry.summary: Provides the first convergence analysis for training transformer-based diffusion models on multi-token Gaussian mixture data, showing why gradient methods converge to optimal denoisers despite non-convex landscapes.

entry.title: Replicable Composition

author.name: Kiarash Banihashem, MohammadHossein Bateni, Hossein Esfandiari, Samira Goudarzi, MohammadTaghi Hajiaghayi

entry.summary: Resolves an open problem in replicable composition: shows that k problems with sample complexities n1,...,nk can be jointly solved with O(sum ni + k) samples while preserving replicability, achieving optimal scaling. Previous best was O(nk²) or O(n²k).

entry.title: UniToolCall: Unifying Tool-Use Representation, Data, and Evaluation for LLM Agents

author.name: Yijuan Liang, Xinghao Chen, Yifan Ge, Ziyi Wu, Hao Wu, Changyu Zeng, Wei Xing, Xiaoyu Shen

entry.summary: Presents UniToolCall, a unified framework for tool learning that standardizes toolset construction, dataset generation, and evaluation. Curates 22k+ tools and 390k+ training instances from 10 standardized public datasets plus synthetic data.

entry.title: Deliberative Alignment is Deep, but Uncertainty Remains: Inference time safety improvement in reasoning via attribution of unsafe behavior to base model

author.name: Pankayaraj Pathmanathan, Furong Huang

entry.summary: Studies deliberative alignment (distilling reasoning capabilities from stronger models for safety) and finds alignment gaps between teacher and student models. Shows deliberatively aligned models may exhibit overconfidence in safety refusals.

entry.title: Calibration Collapse Under Sycophancy Fine-Tuning: How Reward Hacking Breaks Uncertainty Quantification in LLMs

author.name: Subramanyam Sahoo

entry.summary: Demonstrates that sycophantic RLHF/GRPO fine-tuning produces severe calibration collapse in LLMs, with near-chance reliability on MMLU. Shows the tension between human preference optimization and uncertainty quantification.

entry.title: AI Achieves a Perfect LSAT Score

author.name: Bonmu Ku

entry.summary: Reports the first documented perfect LSAT score by an AI model. Shows that thinking traces are critical (ablation drops accuracy 8pp), and that distilled models plateau far below frontier despite similar traces. A process reward model narrows the gap.

entry.title: Hodoscope: Unsupervised Monitoring for AI Misbehaviors

author.name: Ziqian Zhong, Shashwat Saxena, Aditi Raghunathan

entry.summary: Presents Hodoscope, an unsupervised monitoring approach for AI agent misbehaviors that discovers problematic behaviors without predefined categories. Identifies distinctive behaviors by detecting actions absent from well-behaved baselines.

entry.title: PAC-BENCH: Evaluating Multi-Agent Collaboration under Privacy Constraints

author.name: Minjun Park, Donghyun Kim, Hyeonjong Ju, Seungwon Lim, Dongwook Choi, Taeyoon Kwon, Minju Kim, Jinyoung Yeo

entry.summary: Presents PAC-Bench, a benchmark for evaluating multi-agent collaboration under privacy constraints. Shows that privacy constraints substantially degrade collaboration performance and create asymmetric dependence on the initiating agent.

entry.title: Conflicts Make Large Reasoning Models Vulnerable to Attacks

author.name: Honghao Liu, Chengjin Xu, Xuhui Jiang, Cehao Yang, Shengming Yin, Zhengwu Ma, Lionel Ni, Jian Guo

entry.summary: Studies how conflicts (internal alignment conflicts and dilemmas) increase attack success rates against Large Reasoning Models, finding that even simple single-round prompts exploiting conflicts can bypass safety alignment.

entry.title: RTMC: Step-Level Credit Assignment via Rollout Trees

author.name: Tao Wang, Suhang Zheng, Xiaoxiao Xu

entry.summary: Introduces Rollout-Tree Monte Carlo (RTMC) for step-level credit assignment in RL, aggregating return statistics across rollouts sharing common states to produce per-step advantages without a learned critic. Bridges gap between GRPO and value-network approaches.

entry.title: Layerwise Dynamics for In-Context Classification in Transformers

author.name: Patrick Lutz, Themistoklis Haris, Arjun Chandra, Aditya Gangrade, Venkatesh Saligrama

entry.summary: Studies in-context classification in transformers by enforcing feature/label-permutation equivariance, extracting an explicit depth-indexed recursion as the emergent update rule. First identified end-to-end emergent update rule inside a softmax transformer.

entry.title: Discrete Flow Maps

author.name: Peter Potaptchik, Jason Yim, Adhi Saravanan, Peter Holderrieth, Eric Vanden-Eijnden, Michael S. Albergo

entry.summary: Proposes Discrete Flow Maps that compress generative trajectories into single-step mappings for text generation, resolving the geometric mismatch between Euclidean regression and probability simplex. Enables parallel generation bypassing autoregressive bottleneck.

entry.title: Agentic Aggregation for Parallel Scaling of Long-Horizon Agentic Tasks

author.name: Yoonsang Lee, Howard Yen, Xi Ye, Danqi Chen

entry.summary: Studies parallel test-time scaling for long-horizon agentic tasks and proposes AggAgent, an aggregation agent that inspects and searches across parallel trajectories using lightweight tools, rather than just aggregating final answers.

entry.title: Agentic Exploration of PDE Spaces using Latent Foundation Models for Parameterized Simulations

author.name: Abhijeet Vishwasrao, Francisco Giral, Mahmoud Golestanian, Federica Tonti, Andrea Arroyo Ramo, Adrian Lozano-Duran, Steven L. Brunton, Sergio Hoyas, Soledad Le Clainche, Hector Gomez, Ricardo Vinuesa

entry.summary: Couples multi-agent LLMs with latent foundation models to explore PDE solution spaces for physics simulations, enabling automated large-scale exploration of parameterized simulations. Addresses the gap between continuous physical phenomena and discrete LLM interfaces.

entry.title: Controllable and Verifiable Tool-Use Data Synthesis for Agentic Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Siyuan Xu, Shiyang Li, Xin Liu, Tianyi Liu, Yixiao Li, Zhan Shi, Zixuan Zhang, Zilong Wang, Qingyu Yin, Jianshu Chen, Tuo Zhao, Bing Yin

entry.summary: COVERT is a two-stage pipeline for generating tool-use training data for RL, creating reliable base trajectories with multi-level validation then applying oracle-preserving augmentations to increase complexity. Enables automatic reward computation.

entry.title: Tracing the Roots: A Multi-Agent Framework for Uncovering Data Lineage in Post-Training LLMs

author.name: Yu Li, Xiaoran Shang, Qizhi Pei, Yun Zhu, Xin Gao, Honglin Lin, Zhanping Zhong, Zhuoshi Pan, Zheng Liu, Xiaoyang Wang, Conghui He, Dahua Lin, Feng Zhao, Lijun Wu

entry.summary: Introduces the concept of 'data lineage' for LLM training datasets and proposes a multi-agent framework to automatically reconstruct how datasets evolved, revealing structural redundancy and domain-specific patterns. Identifies systemic issues like implicit dataset contamination.

entry.title: Agent^2 RL-Bench: Can LLM Agents Engineer Agentic RL Post-Training?

author.name: Wanyi Chen, Xiao Yang, Xu Yang, Tianming Sha, Qizheng Li, Zhuo Wang, Bowen Xian, Fang Kong, Weiqing Liu, Jiang Bian

entry.summary: Introduces Agent²RL-Bench, a benchmark testing whether LLM agents can autonomously design, implement, and run complete RL post-training pipelines. Features six tasks across three difficulty levels from static rule-based to closed-loop online RL.

entry.title: Three Roles, One Model: Role Orchestration at Inference Time to Close the Performance Gap Between Small and Large Agents

author.name: S. Aaron McClendon, Jorge Gallego-Feliciano, Stavros Zervoudakis, Antonios Saravanos

entry.summary: Demonstrates that inference-time scaffolding (deploying the same frozen small model in three distinct roles) can dramatically improve tool-use performance of small LLMs on a single 24GB GPU. Qwen3-8B goes from ~5% to much higher task completion without any training. Practical approach to democratizing capable AI agents on modest hardware.

entry.title: SWE-AGILE: A Software Agent Framework for Efficiently Managing Dynamic Reasoning Context

author.name: Shuquan Lian, Juncheng Liu, Yazhe Chen, Yuhong Chen, Hui Li

entry.summary: Introduces SWE-AGILE, a software engineering agent framework that manages dynamic reasoning context to balance reasoning depth, efficiency, and context constraints. Addresses the dilemma of retaining vs. discarding reasoning history in multi-turn SWE tasks.

entry.title: Grid2Matrix: Revealing Digital Agnosia in Vision-Language Models

author.name: Yunkai Zhang, Linda Li, Yingxin Cui, Xiyuan Ruan, Zeyu Zheng, Kezhen Chen, Yi Zhang, Diji Yang

entry.summary: Introduces Grid2Matrix (G2M), a controlled benchmark revealing 'digital agnosia' in Vision-Language Models - a sharp early collapse in reading color grids rather than gradual degradation, pointing to fundamental limitations in visual encoders.

entry.title: The Rise and Fall of $G$ in AGI

author.name: David C. Krakauer

entry.summary: Connects Spearman's g-factor from psychometrics to claims about AGI by applying PCA to a models×benchmarks×time matrix spanning 39 models and 14 benchmarks, finding a strong positive manifold.

entry.title: Early Decisions Matter: Proximity Bias and Initial Trajectory Shaping in Non-Autoregressive Diffusion Language Models

author.name: Jiyeon Kim, Sungik Choi, Yongrae Jo, Moontae Lee, Minjoon Seo

entry.summary: Uncovers proximity bias in diffusion language models' non-autoregressive decoding where denoising concentrates on spatially adjacent tokens, leading to poor reasoning. Proposes trajectory shaping to mitigate this.

entry.title: Efficient Process Reward Modeling via Contrastive Mutual Information

author.name: Nakyung Lee, Sangwoo Hong, Jungwoo Lee

entry.summary: Proposes efficient process reward modeling via contrastive pointwise mutual information (CPMI), using model internal probabilities for step-level reward labeling instead of expensive human annotation or Monte Carlo estimation.

entry.title: Pseudo-Unification: Entropy Probing Reveals Divergent Information Patterns in Unified Multimodal Models

author.name: Songlin Yang, Xianghao Kong, Anyi Rao

entry.summary: Identifies and diagnoses 'pseudo-unification' in unified multimodal models (UMMs) - where models fail to transfer LLM reasoning to image synthesis. Proposes an information-theoretic probing framework revealing that understanding and generation pathways encode information divergently.

entry.title: Quantization Dominates Rank Reduction for KV-Cache Compression

author.name: Samuel Salfati

entry.summary: Systematically compares quantization vs rank reduction for KV-cache compression across models from 124M to 14B parameters, finding quantization consistently dominates. Traces the gap to a structural asymmetry under softmax attention where removing dimensions can flip routing.

entry.title: Continuous Adversarial Flow Models

author.name: Shanchuan Lin, Ceyuan Yang, Zhijie Lin, Hao Chen, Haoqi Fan

entry.summary: Proposes continuous adversarial flow models that replace MSE loss in flow matching with a learned discriminator. Post-training improves guidance-free FID on ImageNet 256px from 8.26 to 3.63 for SiT and 7.17 to 3.57 for JiT.

entry.title: Attention Sinks as Internal Signals for Hallucination Detection in Large Language Models

author.name: Jakub Binkowski, Kamil Adamczewski, Tomasz Kajdanowicz

entry.summary: Proposes SinkProbe, a hallucination detection method grounded in attention sinks—tokens that accumulate disproportionate attention mass during generation, indicating a shift from input-grounded to prior-dominated computation.

entry.title: Weird Generalization is Weirdly Brittle

author.name: Miriam Wanner, Hannah Collison, William Jurayj, Benjamin Van Durme, Mark Dredze, William Walden

entry.summary: Presents an extended replication study of weird generalization (where narrow domain fine-tuning causes surprising out-of-domain behavior changes). Finds the phenomenon is exceptionally brittle, emerging only for specific model-dataset combinations and vanishing under simple interventions.

entry.title: Lost in Diffusion: Uncovering Hallucination Patterns and Failure Modes in Diffusion Large Language Models

author.name: Zhengnan Guo, Fei Tan

entry.summary: First controlled comparative study of hallucination patterns in Diffusion Large Language Models (dLLMs) vs autoregressive models. Finds dLLMs hallucinate more, with divergent inference-time dynamics between sequential and non-sequential decoding.

entry.title: Relax: An Asynchronous Reinforcement Learning Engine for Omni-Modal Post-Training at Scale

author.name: Liujie Zhang, Benzhe Ning, Rui Yang, Xiaoyan Yu, Jiaxing Li, Lumeng Wu, Jia Liu, Minghao Li, Weihang Chen, Weiqi Hu, Lei Zhang

entry.summary: Presents Relax, an open-source RL training engine for omni-modal post-training that addresses heterogeneous data flows, operational robustness, and staleness-throughput tradeoffs through three co-designed architectural layers.

entry.title: Any 3D Scene is Worth 1K Tokens: 3D-Grounded Representation for Scene Generation at Scale

author.name: Dongxu Wei, Qi Xu, Zhiqi Li, Hangning Zhou, Cong Qiu, Hailong Qin, Mu Yang, Zhaopeng Cui, Peidong Liu

entry.summary: Proposes the first approach to perform 3D scene generation directly in a 3D-grounded latent space using only ~1K tokens per scene, avoiding the redundancy and inconsistency of 2D-based diffusion approaches. Addresses fundamental limitations of view-based 3D generation.

entry.title: MLLM-as-a-Judge Exhibits Model Preference Bias

author.name: Shuitsu Koyama, Yuiga Wada, Daichi Yashima, Komei Sugiura

entry.summary: Philautia-Eval investigates model-specific preference bias in MLLM-as-a-Judge evaluation, finding that MLLMs tend to exhibit self-preference bias. Uses 1.29M caption-score pairs from 12 MLLMs to quantify this bias.

entry.title: Only Law Can Prevent Extinction

author.name: Eliezer Yudkowsky

entry.summary: Yudkowsky argues that only law—predictable, avoidable state-backed enforcement—can prevent AI-driven extinction, distinguishing between state violence (predictable, avoidable) and banditry, and arguing that international legal frameworks are necessary to constrain AI development.

entry.title: What do your logits know? (The answer may surprise you!)

author.name: Masha Fedzechkina, Eleonora Gualdoni, Rita Ramos, Sinead Williamson

entry.summary: Systematically compares information retained at different representational levels in VLMs—from residual streams through tuned lens projections to final logits—revealing that even easily accessible bottlenecks retain significant information, posing privacy risks.

entry.title: LoopGuard: Breaking Self-Reinforcing Attention Loops via Dynamic KV Cache Intervention

author.name: Dongjie Xu, Hao Wu, Weijie Shi, Yue Cui, Yuanjun Liu, Jiawei Li, Haolun Ma, An Liu, Jia Zhu, Jiajie Xu

entry.summary: LoopGuard identifies and addresses a failure mode where LLM decoding collapses into repetition loops driven by collapsed attention patterns, exacerbated by KV cache reuse. Introduces LoopBench for studying this systematically.

entry.title: The Amazing Agent Race: Strong Tool Users, Weak Navigators

author.name: Zae Myung Kim, Dongseok Lee, Jaehyung Kim, Vipul Raheja, Dongyeop Kang

entry.summary: The Amazing Agent Race (AAR) benchmark introduces DAG-structured tool-use puzzles with fork-merge chains, addressing the limitation that 55-100% of existing benchmark instances are simple linear chains. Evaluates agents on 1,400 instances across difficulty levels.

entry.title: Sanity Checks for Agentic Data Science

author.name: Zachary T. Rewolinski, Austin V. Zane, Hao Huang, Chandan Singh, Chenglong Wang, Jianfeng Gao, Bin Yu

entry.summary: Proposes sanity checks for agentic data science (ADS) pipelines grounded in the PCS framework. Uses perturbation-based checks to screen whether agents can reliably distinguish signal from noise, exposing falsely optimistic conclusions.

entry.title: Escaping the Context Bottleneck: Active Context Curation for LLM Agents via Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Xiaozhe Li, Tianyi Lyu, Yizhao Yang, Liang Shan, Siyi Yang, Ligao Zhang, Zhuoyi Huang, Qingwen Liu, Yang Li

entry.summary: Proposes ContextCurator, a lightweight RL-trained policy model that actively curates context for a frozen foundation model during long-horizon tasks. Aggressively prunes environmental noise while preserving 'reasoning anchors' critical for future deductions.

entry.title: LLM Nepotism in Organizational Governance

author.name: Shunqi Mao, Wei Guo, Dingxin Zhang, Chaoyi Zhang, Weidong Cai

entry.summary: Studies 'LLM Nepotism' - a bias where LLM evaluators reward candidates who express favorable attitudes toward AI in resume screening and governance decisions, even when irrelevant to merit.

entry.title: Do We Still Need GraphRAG? Benchmarking RAG and GraphRAG for Agentic Search Systems

author.name: Dongzhe Fan, Zheyi Xue, Siyuan Liu, Qiaoyu Tan

entry.summary: Benchmarks RAG vs GraphRAG in the context of agentic search systems with dynamic multi-round retrieval. Questions whether explicit graph structure is needed when agentic search can compensate through interaction.

entry.title: Critical-CoT: A Robust Defense Framework against Reasoning-Level Backdoor Attacks in Large Language Models

author.name: Vu Tuan Truong, Long Bao Le

entry.summary: Proposes Critical-CoT, a defense against reasoning-level backdoor attacks in LLMs that insert malicious reasoning steps into chain-of-thought. First defense specifically targeting CoT-level backdoors.

entry.title: Rethinking Token-Level Credit Assignment in RLVR: A Polarity-Entropy Analysis

author.name: Yuhang He, Haodong Wu, Siyi Liu, Hongyu Ge, Hange Zhou, Keyi Wu, Zhuo Zheng, Qihong Lin, Zixin Zhong, Yongqi Zhang

entry.summary: Analyzes token-level credit assignment in RLVR through reward polarity and token entropy, proving that credit a token can carry is upper-bounded by its entropy. Proposes the Four Quadrant Decomposition diagnostic tool and derives practical training strategies.

entry.title: The Salami Slicing Threat: Exploiting Cumulative Risks in LLM Systems

author.name: Yihao Zhang, Kai Wang, Jiangrong Wu, Haolin Wu, Yuxuan Zhou, Zeming Wei, Dongxian Wu, Xun Chen, Jun Sun, Meng Sun

entry.summary: Proposes the 'salami slicing' threat model for LLM jailbreaking where each individual interaction appears benign but cumulative interactions achieve harmful goals. Addresses limitations of existing multi-turn attacks that use explicit harmful triggers.

entry.title: FM-Agent: Scaling Formal Methods to Large Systems via LLM-Based Hoare-Style Reasoning

author.name: Haoran Ding, Zhaoguo Wang, Haibo Chen

entry.summary: Presents FM-Agent, an LLM-based system for scaling formal verification to large systems using Hoare-style compositional reasoning. Automates writing formal specifications for each function, addressing the human burden of formal methods.

entry.title: A Mechanistic Analysis of Looped Reasoning Language Models

author.name: Hugh Blayney, \'Alvaro Arroyo, Johan Obando-Ceron, Pablo Samuel Castro, Aaron Courville, Michael M. Bronstein, Xiaowen Dong

entry.summary: Conducts mechanistic analysis of looped reasoning language models, showing each layer in the cycle converges to a distinct fixed point. Compares inference stage dynamics between feedforward and looped models.

entry.title: OccuBench: Evaluating AI Agents on Real-World Professional Tasks via Language World Models

author.name: Xiaomeng Hu, Yinger Zhang, Fei Huang, Jianhong Tu, Yang Su, Lianghao Deng, Yuxuan Liu, Yantao Liu, Dayiheng Liu, Tsung-Yi Ho

entry.summary: Introduces OccuBench, a benchmark covering 100 professional task scenarios across 65 domains using Language World Models to simulate environments. Enables evaluating AI agents in domains where real environments don't exist.

entry.title: Decomposing and Reducing Hidden Measurement Error in LLM Evaluation Pipelines

author.name: Solomon Messing

entry.summary: Decomposes hidden measurement error in LLM evaluation pipelines, showing that prompt rephrasing, judge model choice, and temperature can flip model rankings. Distinguishes variance that shrinks with data from researcher design choices.

entry.title: SinkTrack: Attention Sink based Context Anchoring for Large Language Models

author.name: Xu Liu, Guikun Chen, Wenguan Wang

entry.summary: SinkTrack exploits the attention sink phenomenon in LLMs to anchor contextual information by injecting key features into the first token's representation, reducing hallucination and context forgetting.

entry.title: LottieGPT: Tokenizing Vector Animation for Autoregressive Generation

author.name: Junhao Chen, Kejun Gao, Yuehan Cui, Mingze Sun, Mingjin Chen, Shaohui Wang, Xiaoxiao Long, Fei Ma, Qi Tian, Ruqi Huang, Hao Zhao

entry.summary: LottieGPT presents the first framework for tokenizing and autoregressively generating vector animations (Lottie format), extending large multimodal models to structured vector animation synthesis.

entry.title: Evaluating Reliability Gaps in Large Language Model Safety via Repeated Prompt Sampling

author.name: Keita Broadwater

entry.summary: Introduces Accelerated Prompt Stress Testing (APST), a framework that probes LLM safety by repeatedly sampling the same prompt under controlled conditions, inspired by reliability engineering. Focuses on consistency under repeated use rather than breadth of tasks.

entry.title: COMPOSITE-Stem

author.name: Kyle Waters, Lucas Nuzzi, Tadhg Looram, Alessandro Tomasiello, Ariel Ghislain Kemogne Kamdoum, Bikun Li, Damien Sileo, Egor Kretov, Francesco Fournier-Facio, Georgios Soloupis, Haile Kassahun, Hew Wolff, Jiaqi Cai, Lianghui Li, Marc Roth, Mohinder Naiya, Naixu Guo, Qicheng Tang, Richard Wheeler, Samuele Sala, Serguei Popov, Steven Dillman, Yuqi Li

entry.summary: COMPOSITE-STEM is a benchmark of 70 expert-written tasks across physics, biology, chemistry, and math, curated by doctoral researchers. Uses LLM-as-jury grading with rubrics for flexible assessment of scientifically meaningful outputs.

entry.title: Instructing LLMs to Negotiate using Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards

author.name: Shuze Daniel Liu, Claire Chen, Jiabao Sean Xiao, Lei Lei, Yuheng Zhang, Yisong Yue, David Simchi-Levi

entry.summary: Investigates using Reinforcement Learning from Verifiable Rewards (RLVR) to teach LLMs to negotiate in bilateral price bargaining. Discovers a novel four-phase behavioral emergence during training with economically grounded rewards.

entry.title: Cognitive Pivot Points and Visual Anchoring: Unveiling and Rectifying Hallucinations in Multimodal Reasoning Models

author.name: Zhe Qian, Yanbiao Ma, Zhuohan Ouyang, Zhonghua Wang, Zhongxing Xu, Fei Luo, Xinyu Liu, Zongyuan Ge, Yike Guo, Jungong Han

entry.summary: Identifies 'Reasoning Vision Truth Disconnect' in multimodal reasoning models where hallucinations correlate with high-entropy cognitive bifurcation points. Proposes visual anchoring interventions at intermediate layers to address the breakdown.

entry.title: TrajOnco: a multi-agent framework for temporal reasoning over longitudinal EHR for multi-cancer early detection

author.name: Sihang Zeng, Young Won Kim, Wilson Lau, Ehsan Alipour, Ruth Etzioni, Meliha Yetisgen, Anand Oka

entry.summary: TrajOnco is a training-free multi-agent LLM framework for early cancer detection from longitudinal EHRs, performing temporal reasoning over clinical events across 15 cancer types. Uses chain-of-agents with long-term memory.

entry.title: Thinking Fast, Thinking Wrong: Intuitiveness Modulates LLM Counterfactual Reasoning in Policy Evaluation

author.name: Yanjie He

entry.summary: Constructs a benchmark of 40 empirical policy evaluation cases to test LLM counterfactual reasoning. Discovers a 'chain-of-thought paradox' where CoT prompting can actually hurt performance on counter-intuitive cases, revealing LLMs' reliance on prior expectations rather than genuine causal reasoning.

entry.title: SciPredict: Can LLMs Predict the Outcomes of Scientific Experiments in Natural Sciences?

author.name: Udari Madhushani Sehwag, Elaine Lau, Haniyeh Ehsani Oskouie, Shayan Shabihi, Erich Liang, Andrea Toledo, Guillermo Mangialardi, Sergio Fonrouge, Ed-Yeremai Hernandez Cardona, Paula Vergara, Utkarsh Tyagi, Chen Bo Calvin Zhang, Pavi Bhatter, Nicholas Johnson, Furong Huang, Ernesto Gabriel Hernandez Montoya, Bing Liu

entry.summary: Introduces SciPredict, a benchmark of 405 tasks from 33 sub-fields of physics, biology, and chemistry to evaluate whether LLMs can predict experimental outcomes. Tests whether such predictions can reliably guide scientific resource allocation.

entry.title: ZoomR: Memory Efficient Reasoning through Multi-Granularity Key Value Retrieval

author.name: David H. Yang, Yuxuan Zhu, Mohammad Mohammadi Amiri, Keerthiram Murugesan, Tejaswini Pedapati, Subhajit Chaudhury, Pin-Yu Chen

entry.summary: Introduces ZoomR, an approach for compressing KV cache during long reasoning by adaptively summarizing verbose thoughts and using dynamic KV cache selection. Targets the memory bottleneck of long output generation rather than long input context.

entry.title: WebForge: Breaking the Realism-Reproducibility-Scalability Trilemma in Browser Agent Benchmark

author.name: Peng Yuan, Yuyang Yin, Yuxuan Cai, Zheng Wei

entry.summary: Presents WebForge, a fully automated framework resolving the realism-reproducibility-scalability trilemma in browser agent benchmarks through a four-agent pipeline that produces interactive web environments without human annotation.

entry.title: Persona Non Grata: Single-Method Safety Evaluation Is Incomplete for Persona-Imbued LLMs

author.name: Wenkai Li, Fan Yang, Shaunak A. Mehta, Koichi Onoue

entry.summary: Shows that prompting and activation steering expose different, architecture-dependent vulnerability profiles in persona-imbued LLMs. Testing with only one method can miss a model's dominant failure mode. Tests across 5,568 conditions on four models.

entry.title: PaperScope: A Multi-Modal Multi-Document Benchmark for Agentic Deep Research Across Massive Scientific Papers

author.name: Lei Xiong, Huaying Yuan, Zheng Liu, Zhao Cao, Zhicheng Dou

entry.summary: Introduces PaperScope, a multi-modal multi-document benchmark for evaluating AI systems on deep scientific research tasks. Built on a knowledge graph of 2,000+ AI papers requiring integration of text, tables, and figures across multiple documents.

entry.title: OOM-RL: Out-of-Money Reinforcement Learning Market-Driven Alignment for LLM-Based Multi-Agent Systems

author.name: Kun Liu, Liqun Chen

entry.summary: Proposes OOM-RL (Out-of-Money Reinforcement Learning), using live financial markets as an alignment signal for multi-agent systems. Capital depletion serves as an 'un-hackable' negative gradient. Includes a 20-month longitudinal study from July 2024 to February 2026.

entry.title: Problem Reductions at Scale: Agentic Integration of Computationally Hard Problems

author.name: Xi-Wei Pan, Shi-Wen An, Jin-Guo Liu

entry.summary: Uses AI coding agents with 'harness engineering' to build a large-scale library of polynomial-time reductions between NP-hard problems, enabling practitioners to route any problem to any solver through a single interface.

entry.title: Fairboard: a quantitative framework for equity assessment of healthcare models

author.name: James K. Ruffle, Samia Mohinta, Chris Foulon, Mohamad Zeina, Zicheng Wang, Sebastian Brandner, Harpreet Hyare, Parashkev Nachev

entry.summary: Presents Fairboard, a quantitative framework for equity assessment of healthcare AI models, evaluating 18 brain tumor segmentation models across 648 patients. Finds patient identity explains more performance variance than model choice.

entry.title: A Comparative Theoretical Analysis of Entropy Control Methods in Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Ming Lei, Christophe Baehr

entry.summary: Provides theoretical analysis comparing entropy control strategies in RL for LLMs - traditional entropy regularization vs. covariance-based mechanisms. Shows entropy dynamics are governed by covariance between log-probabilities and logit updates.

entry.title: MPAC: A Multi-Principal Agent Coordination Protocol for Interoperable Multi-Agent Collaboration

author.name: Kaiyang Qian, Xinmin Fang, Zhengxiong Li

entry.summary: Proposes MPAC, a Multi-Principal Agent Coordination Protocol that addresses the gap between MCP (tool invocation) and A2A (single-principal delegation) when independent principals' agents must coordinate over shared state.

entry.title: Is There Knowledge Left to Extract? Evidence of Fragility in Medically Fine-Tuned Vision-Language Models

author.name: Oliver McLaughlin, Daniel Shubin, Carsten Eickhoff, Ritambhara Singh, William Rudman, Michal Golovanevsky

entry.summary: Evaluates medical fine-tuning of VLMs (LLaVA-Med, MedGemma), finding performance degrades to near-random on difficult tasks, medical fine-tuning provides no consistent advantage, and models are highly sensitive to prompt formulation.

entry.title: Muon$^2$: Boosting Muon via Adaptive Second-Moment Preconditioning

author.name: Ziyue Liu, Ruijie Zhang, Zhengyang Wang, Yequan Zhao, Yupeng Su, Zi Yang, Zheng Zhang

entry.summary: Proposes Muon², extending the Muon optimizer with Adam-style adaptive second-moment preconditioning before orthogonalization, improving the conditioning of the momentum matrix and reducing required Newton-Schulz iterations.

entry.title: Machine Learning-Based Detection of MCP Attacks

author.name: Tobias Mattsson, Samuel Nyberg, Anton Borg, Ricardo Britto

entry.summary: First study on ML-based detection of malicious MCP (Model Context Protocol) tool descriptions, evaluating both traditional and deep learning classifiers for binary and multiclass attack identification.

entry.title: Computational Lesions in Multilingual Language Models Separate Shared and Language-specific Brain Alignment

author.name: Yang Cui, Jingyuan Sun, Yizheng Sun, Yifan Wang, Yunhao Zhang, Jixing Li, Shaonan Wang, Hongpeng Zhou, John Hale, Chengqing Zong, Goran Nenadic

entry.summary: Uses computational lesions in multilingual LLMs to separate shared vs. language-specific brain alignment, comparing intact and lesioned models against fMRI responses during story listening in English, Chinese, and French.

entry.title: Audio-Omni: Extending Multi-modal Understanding to Versatile Audio Generation and Editing

author.name: Zeyue Tian, Binxin Yang, Zhaoyang Liu, Jiexuan Zhang, Ruibin Yuan, Hubery Yin, Qifeng Chen, Chen Li, Jing Lv, Wei Xue, Yike Guo

entry.summary: Introduces Audio-Omni, the first end-to-end framework unifying audio generation and editing across sound, music, and speech domains with integrated multimodal understanding capabilities.

entry.title: Detecting RAG Extraction Attack via Dual-Path Runtime Integrity Game

author.name: Yuanbo Xie, Yingjie Zhang, Yulin Li, Shouyou Song, Xiaokun Chen, Zhihan Liu, Liya Su, Tingwen Liu

entry.summary: Proposes CanaryRAG, a runtime defense against RAG knowledge base extraction attacks inspired by stack canaries, embedding canary tokens in retrieved chunks to detect leakage through a dual-path integrity game.

entry.title: When Verification Fails: How Compositionally Infeasible Claims Escape Rejection

author.name: Muxin Liu, Delip Rao, Grace Kim, Chris Callison-Burch

entry.summary: Exposes a shortcut in scientific claim verification benchmarks where models can pass by checking only the most salient constraint rather than all constraints. Shows existing benchmarks cannot distinguish rigorous verification from salient-constraint checking.

entry.title: EmbodiedGovBench: A Benchmark for Governance, Recovery, and Upgrade Safety in Embodied Agent Systems

author.name: Xue Qin, Simin Luan, John See, Cong Yang, Zhijun Li

entry.summary: Introduces EmbodiedGovBench, a benchmark evaluating whether embodied AI systems are governable - measuring policy compliance, recovery, auditability, and human oversight rather than just task success. Tests governance properties of robot systems.

entry.title: Low-rank Optimization Trajectories Modeling for LLM RLVR Acceleration

author.name: Zhipeng Chen, Tao Qian, Wayne Xin Zhao, Ji-Rong Wen

entry.summary: Studies optimization trajectories during RLVR training of LLMs and finds that rank-1 subspace evolution is nonlinear. Proposes low-rank trajectory modeling to accelerate RLVR training by reducing computational overhead of extensive exploration.

entry.title: Playing Along: Learning a Double-Agent Defender for Belief Steering via Theory of Mind

author.name: Hanqi Xiao, Vaidehi Patil, Zaid Khan, Hyunji Lee, Elias Stengel-Eskin, Mohit Bansal

entry.summary: Proposes ToM-SB, a privacy-themed Theory of Mind challenge where a defender must act as a double agent to steer attacker beliefs. Tests frontier LLMs' ability to form and use theory of mind for safe interaction with adversarial partners.

entry.title: When Can You Poison Rewards? A Tight Characterization of Reward Poisoning in Linear MDPs

author.name: Jose Efraim Aguilar Escamilla, Haoyang Hong, Jiawei Li, Haoyu Zhao, Xuezhou Zhang, Sanghyun Hong, Huazheng Wang

entry.summary: Provides the first precise necessity and sufficiency characterization of attackability of linear MDPs under reward poisoning, drawing a bright line between vulnerable and intrinsically robust RL instances.

entry.title: Tracing the Thought of a Grandmaster-level Chess-Playing Transformer

author.name: Rui Lin, Zhenyu Jin, Guancheng Zhou, Xuyang Ge, Wentao Shu, Jiaxing Wu, Junxuan Wang, Zhengfu He, Junping Zhang, Xipeng Qiu

entry.summary: Introduces a sparse decomposition framework to interpret Leela Chess Zero's internal computation, revealing interpretable tactical considerations and parallel reasoning behavior consistent with its architecture.

entry.title: Transformers Learn Latent Mixture Models In-Context via Mirror Descent

author.name: Francesco D'Angelo, Nicolas Flammarion

entry.summary: Shows that transformers can implement Mirror Descent to learn mixture weights in-context for Mixture of Transition Distributions models. Provides constructive proofs that attention layers can represent this optimization and validates with experiments.

entry.title: Reducing Hallucination in Enterprise AI Workflows via Hybrid Utility Minimum Bayes Risk (HUMBR)

author.name: Chenhao Fang, Jordi Mola, Mark Harman, Jason Nawrocki, Vaibhav Shrivastava, Yue Cheng, Jay Minesh Shah, Katayoun Zand, Mansi Tripathi, Arya Pudota, Matthew Becker, Herv\'e Robert, Abhishek Gulati

entry.summary: Introduces HUMBR from Meta, a Hybrid Utility Minimum Bayes Risk framework combining semantic embedding similarity with lexical precision for LLM hallucination mitigation in high-stakes enterprise workflows like legal and compliance.

entry.title: Tessera: Unlocking Heterogeneous GPUs through Kernel-Granularity Disaggregation

author.name: Tiancheng Hu, Jin Qin, Zheng Wang, Junhao Hu, Yuzheng Wang, Lei Chen, Yizhou Shan, Mingxing Zhang, Ting Cao, Chunwei Xia, Huimin Cui, Tao Xie, Chenxi Wang

entry.summary: Presents Tessera, the first kernel-granularity disaggregation system for heterogeneous GPU clusters in large model inference. Maps individual kernels to different GPU types based on their resource demands for improved performance and cost efficiency.

entry.title: Transactional Attention: Semantic Sponsorship for KV-Cache Retention

author.name: Abhinaba Basu

entry.summary: Introduces Transactional Attention, a sponsorship mechanism where structural anchor tokens protect adjacent value tokens from KV-cache eviction. Achieves 100% credential retrieval at K=16 where all six baselines achieve 0%.

entry.title: Utilizing and Calibrating Hindsight Process Rewards via Reinforcement with Mutual Information Self-Evaluation

author.name: Jiashu Yao, Heyan Huang, Zeming Liu, Yuhang Guo

entry.summary: Proposes MISE, an RL paradigm using mutual information self-evaluation for LLM agents that provides dense reward signals while calibrating against environmental feedback. First formal foundation for generative self-rewarding.

entry.title: Why Supervised Fine-Tuning Fails to Learn: A Systematic Study of Incomplete Learning in Large Language Models

author.name: Chao Xue, Yao Wang, Mengqiao Liu, Di Liang, Xingsheng Han, Peiyang Liu, Xianjie Wu, Chenyao Lu, Lei Jiang, Yu Lu, Haibo Shi, Shuang Liang, Minlong Peng, Flora D. Salim

entry.summary: First systematic study of Incomplete Learning Phenomenon (ILP) in LLM SFT, where converged models fail to reproduce training instances. Identifies five recurrent sources including missing prerequisites and conflicting demonstrations.

entry.title: CodeComp: Structural KV Cache Compression for Agentic Coding

author.name: Qiujiang Chen, Jing Xiong, Chenyang Zhao, Sidi Yang, Ngai Wong

entry.summary: Presents CodeComp, a training-free KV cache compression framework for agentic coding that incorporates static program analysis (Code Property Graphs) into LLM inference. Outperforms attention-only compression on bug localization and code generation.

entry.title: Why Don't You Know? Evaluating the Impact of Uncertainty Sources on Uncertainty Quantification in LLMs

author.name: Maiya Goloburda, Roman Vashurin, Fedor Chernogorsky, Nurkhan Laiyk, Daniil Orel, Preslav Nakov, Maxim Panov

entry.summary: Studies how different sources of uncertainty (knowledge gaps, output variability, input ambiguity) impact the effectiveness of existing uncertainty quantification methods for LLMs. Introduces a controlled dataset for analysis.

entry.title: See Fair, Speak Truth: Equitable Attention Improves Grounding and Reduces Hallucination in Vision-Language Alignment

author.name: Mohammad Anas Azeez, Ankan Deria, Zohaib Hasan Siddiqui, Adinath Madhavrao Dukre, Rafiq Ali, Sara Atito, Yutong Xie, Imran Razzak

entry.summary: DOP-OBC is a training-free decoding strategy for multimodal LLMs that reduces object hallucination by ensuring equitable attention allocation across all objects regardless of size or visual salience.

entry.title: Mining Attribute Subspaces for Efficient Fine-tuning of 3D Foundation Models

author.name: Yu Jiang, Hanwen Jiang, Ahmed Abdelkader, Wen-Sheng Chu, Brandon Y. Feng, Zhangyang Wang, Qixing Huang

entry.summary: Discovers that LoRA fine-tuning subspaces for 3D foundation models can be associated with specific attribute variations (texture, geometry, lighting) and that these subspaces are approximately disentangled.

entry.title: TAPNext++: What's Next for Tracking Any Point (TAP)?

author.name: Sebastian Jung, Artem Zholus, Martin Sundermeyer, Carl Doersch, Ross Goroshin, David Joseph Tan, Sarath Chandar, Rudolph Triebel, Federico Tombari

entry.summary: TAPNext++ extends point tracking to handle much longer video sequences with re-detection of reappearing points after occlusion. From Google/DeepMind researchers (Tombari), it maintains low memory/compute while tracking orders of magnitude longer sequences.

entry.title: Script-a-Video: Deep Structured Audio-visual Captions via Factorized Streams and Relational Grounding

author.name: Tencent Hunyuan Team

entry.summary: Script-a-Video from Tencent Hunyuan proposes Multi-Stream Scene Script (MTSS), replacing monolithic video captions with factorized, explicitly grounded scene descriptions. Decomposes video into separate visual, auditory, and identity streams for better video understanding and generation.

entry.title: NTIRE 2026 Challenge on Robust AI-Generated Image Detection in the Wild

author.name: Aleksandr Gushchin, Khaled Abud, Ekaterina Shumitskaya, Artem Filippov, Georgii Bychkov, Sergey Lavrushkin, Mikhail Erofeev, Anastasia Antsiferova, Changsheng Chen, Shunquan Tan, Radu Timofte, Dmitry Vatolin, Chuanbiao Song, Zijian Yu, Hao Tan, Jun Lan, Zhiqiang Yang, Yongwei Tang, Zhiqiang Wu, Jia Wen Seow, Hong Vin Koay, Haodong Ren, Feng Xu, Shuai Chen, Ruiyang Xia, Qi Zhang, Yaowen Xu, Zhaofan Zou, Hao Sun, Dagong Lu, Mufeng Yao, Xinlei Xu, Fei Wu, Fengjun Guo, Cong Luo, Hardik Sharma, Aashish Negi, Prateek Shaily, Jayant Kumar, Sachin Chaudhary, Akshay Dudhane, Praful Hambarde, Amit Shukla, Zhilin Tu, Fengpeng Li, Jiamin Zhang, Jianwei Fei, Kemou Li, Haiwei Wu, Bilel Benjdira, Anas M. Ali, Wadii Boulila, Chenfan Qu, Junchi Li

entry.summary: Overview of NTIRE 2026 Challenge on robust AI-generated image detection, with a novel dataset of 108K real and 185K AI-generated images from 42 generators with 36 transformations. Establishes comprehensive benchmarks for detecting AI-generated content.

entry.title: Towards Brain MRI Foundation Models for the Clinic: Findings from the FOMO25 Challenge

author.name: Asbj{\o}rn Munk, Stefano Cerri, Vardan Nersesjan, Christian Hedeager Krag, Jakob Ambsdorf, Pablo Rocamora Garc\'ia, Julia Machnio, Peirong Liu, Suhyun Ahn, Nasrin Akbari, Yasmina Al Khalil, Kimberly Amador, Sina Amirrajab, Tal Arbel, Meritxell Bach Cuadra, Ujjwal Baid, Bhakti Baheti, Jaume Banus, Kamil Barbierik, Christoph Brune, Yansong Bu, Baptiste Callard, Yuhan Chen, Cornelius Crijnen, Corentin Dancette, Peter Drotar, Prasad Dutande, Nils D. Forkert, Saurabh Garg, Jakub Gazda, Matej Gazda, Beno\^it G\'erin, Partha Ghosh, Weikang Gong, Pedro M. Gordaliza, Sam Hashemi, Tobias Heimann, Fucang Jia, Jiexin Jiang, Emily Kaczmarek, Chris Kang, Seung Kwan Kang, Mohammad Khazaei, Julien Khlaut, Petros Koutsouvelis, Jae Sung Lee, Yuchong Li, Mengye Lyu, Mingchen Ma, Anant Madabhushi, Klaus H. Maier-Hein, Pierre Manceron, Andr\'es Mart\'inez Mora, Moona Mazher, Felix Meister, Nataliia Molchanova, Steven A. Niederer, Leonard N\"urnberg, Jinah Park, Abdul Qayyum, Jonas Richiardi, Antoine Saporta, Branislav Setlak, Ning Shen, Justin Szeto, Constantin Ulrich, Puru Vaish, Vibujithan Vigneshwaran, Leroy Volmer, Zihao Wang, Siqi Wei, Anthony Winder, Jelmer M. Wolterink, Maxence Wynen, Chang Yang, Si Young Yie, Mostafa Mehdipour Ghazi, Akshay Pai, Espen Jimenez Solem, Sebastian N{\o}rgaard Llambias, Mikael Boesen, Michael Eriksen Benros, Juan Eugenio Iglesias, Mads Nielsen

entry.summary: FOMO25 challenge for brain MRI foundation models provides FOMO60K pretraining dataset and clinical benchmarks. Evaluates self-supervised learning approaches for clinical brain MRI analysis where labels are scarce.

entry.title: ClawGuard: A Runtime Security Framework for Tool-Augmented LLM Agents Against Indirect Prompt Injection

author.name: Wei Zhao, Zhe Li, Peixin Zhang, Jun Sun

entry.summary: Introduces ClawGuard, a runtime security framework protecting tool-augmented LLM agents against indirect prompt injection by enforcing user-confirmed rule sets at tool-call boundaries.

entry.title: CONSCIENTIA: Can LLM Agents Learn to Strategize? Emergent Deception and Trust in a Multi-Agent NYC Simulation

author.name: Aarush Sinha, Arion Das, Soumyadeep Nag, Charan Karnati, Shravani Nag, Chandra Vadhan Raj, Aman Chadha, Vinija Jain, Suranjana Trivedy, Amitava Das

entry.summary: Constructs a large-scale NYC simulation where LLM agents exhibit emergent strategic behaviors including deception and trust under opposing incentives, studying alignment implications of autonomous agent deployment.

entry.title: Skill-SD: Skill-Conditioned Self-Distillation for Multi-turn LLM Agents

author.name: Hao Wang, Guozhi Wang, Han Xiao, Yufeng Zhou, Yue Pan, Jichao Wang, Ke Xu, Yafei Wen, Xiaohu Ruan, Xiaoxin Chen, Honggang Qi

entry.summary: Proposes Skill-SD for multi-turn LLM agents, turning completed trajectories into compact natural language skills for dynamic self-distillation supervision, addressing sparse reward and training collapse in RL.

entry.title: Test-time Scaling over Perception: Resolving the Grounding Paradox in Thinking with Images

author.name: Zheng Jiang, Yiming Chen, Nan He, Jiahui Chen, Chaoyang Li, Houde Qian, Lifeng Sun

entry.summary: Identifies the 'Grounding Paradox' in multimodal LLMs that think with images: models must decide where to look before having evidence to make that decision. Proposes Test-Time Scaling over Perception (TTSP) with exploratory perception traces and entropy-based filtering.

entry.title: UNIGEOCLIP: Unified Geospatial Contrastive Learning

author.name: Guillaume Astruc, Eduard Trulls, Jan Hosang, Loic Landrieu, Paul-Edouard Sarlin

entry.summary: UNIGEOCLIP aligns five geospatial modalities (aerial imagery, street views, elevation, text, coordinates) in a unified embedding space through all-to-all contrastive learning. Enables cross-modal retrieval and reasoning across arbitrary modality combinations.

entry.title: Turing Test on Screen: A Benchmark for Mobile GUI Agent Humanization

author.name: Jiachen Zhu, Lingyu Yang, Rong Shan, Congmin Zheng, Zeyu Zheng, Weiwen Liu, Yong Yu, Weinan Zhang, Jianghao Lin

entry.summary: Introduces the 'Turing Test on Screen' concept, studying whether GUI agents can be detected as non-human based on their interaction patterns (touch dynamics, kinematics). Creates a benchmark for agent 'humanization' to evade detection on mobile platforms.

entry.title: DeepReviewer 2.0: A Traceable Agentic System for Auditable Scientific Peer Review

author.name: Yixuan Weng, Minjun Zhu, Qiujie Xie, Zhiyuan Ning, Shichen Li, Panzhong Lu, Zhen Lin, Enhao Gu, Qiyao Sun, Yue Zhang

entry.summary: DeepReviewer 2.0 is an agentic peer review system that produces traceable, auditable reviews with anchored annotations and evidence. Evaluated on 134 ICLR 2025 submissions with focus on traceability rather than just fluent critique.

entry.title: Competing with AI Scientists: Agent-Driven Approach to Astrophysics Research

author.name: Thomas Borrett, Licong Xu, Andy Nilipour, Boris Bolliet, Sebastien Pierre, Erwan Allys, Celia Lecat, Biwei Dai, Po-Wen Chang, Wahid Bhimji

entry.summary: Applies a multi-agent AI system (Cmbagent/Denario) to a cosmological parameter inference competition, showing that while fully autonomous performance fell short, human-AI collaboration achieved competitive results.

entry.title: EE-MCP: Self-Evolving MCP-GUI Agents via Automated Environment Generation and Experience Learning

author.name: Tiantian He, Yihang Chen, Keyue Jiang, Ka Yiu Lee, Kaiwen Zhou, Kun Shao, Shuai Wang

entry.summary: EE-MCP proposes a self-evolving framework for agents that combine GUI interaction with API calls via the Model Context Protocol (MCP), learning when each modality provides complementary advantages through automated environment generation.

entry.title: New Hybrid Fine-Tuning Paradigm for LLMs: Algorithm Design and Convergence Analysis Framework

author.name: Shaocong Ma, Peiran Yu, Heng Huang

entry.summary: Proposes a hybrid fine-tuning approach combining zeroth-order and first-order optimization to jointly update full LLM parameters and PEFT modules. Develops theoretical framework based on 'hybrid smoothness' for convergence analysis.

entry.title: SpecMoE: A Fast and Efficient Mixture-of-Experts Inference via Self-Assisted Speculative Decoding

author.name: Jehyeon Bang, Eunyeong Cho, Ranggi Hwang, Jinha Chung, Minsoo Rhu

entry.summary: SpecMoE is a memory-efficient MoE inference system using self-assisted speculative decoding, working without additional model training. Designed to address high memory requirements of MoE models, especially for larger batch sizes.

entry.title: VeriSim: A Configurable Framework for Evaluating Medical AI Under Realistic Patient Noise

author.name: Sina Mansouri, Mohit Marvania, Vibhavari Ashok Shihorkar, Han Ngoc Tran, Kazhal Shafiei, Mehrdad Fazli, Yikuan Li, Ziwei Zhu

entry.summary: VeriSim is a patient simulation framework that injects clinically-grounded noise (memory gaps, health literacy, anxiety) into patient responses while preserving medical ground truth, using UMLS-LLM hybrid verification.

entry.title: FACT-E: Causality-Inspired Evaluation for Trustworthy Chain-of-Thought Reasoning

author.name: Yuxi Sun, Aoqi Zuo, Haotian Xie, Wei Gao, Mingming Gong, Jing Ma

entry.summary: Proposes FACT-E, a causality-inspired framework for evaluating Chain-of-Thought quality. Uses controlled perturbations as instrumental signals to distinguish genuine step-to-step reasoning dependence from bias-driven artifacts, producing more reliable faithfulness estimates.

entry.title: CASK: Core-Aware Selective KV Compression for Reasoning Traces

author.name: Buseong Kim, Heejun Gwon

entry.summary: Proposes CASK, a KV compression method that partitions reasoning traces into a protected core (anchoring answer formation) and mergeable periphery, framing KV compression as behavior-preserving structured consolidation rather than simple eviction.

entry.title: Environmental Footprint of GenAI Research: Insights from the Moshi Foundation Model

author.name: Marta L\'opez-Rauhut, Loic Landrieu, Mathieu Aubry, Anne-Laure Ligozat

entry.summary: Provides detailed environmental footprint analysis of GenAI research through the Moshi foundation model, including often-omitted R&D stages. Reveals that research and development stages contribute significantly beyond final training runs.

entry.title: Learning from Contrasts: Synthesizing Reasoning Paths from Diverse Search Trajectories

author.name: Peiyang Liu, Zhirui Chen, Xi Wang, Di Liang, Youru Li, Zhi Cai, Wei Ye

entry.summary: Introduces Contrastive Reasoning Path Synthesis (CRPS), which transforms MCTS supervision extraction from filtering to synthesis by analyzing differences between high- and low-quality search trajectories to create better reasoning chains.

entry.title: Anthropogenic Regional Adaptation in Multimodal Vision-Language Model

author.name: Samuel Cahyawijaya, Peerat Limkonchotiwat, Tack Hwa Wong, Hitesh Laxmichand Patel, Amit Agarwal, Manuel Antonio Rufino, Carlos Rafael Catalan, Muhammad Reza Qorib, Vicky Feliren, Holy Lovenia, Aye Hninn Khine, Frederikus Hudi, David Anugraha, Alham Fikri Aji, Romrawin Chumpu, Viet-Thanh Pham, Minghan Wang, Mohamed Fazli Imam, Ruochen Zhang, Joseph Marvin Imperial, Do Xuan Long, Musa Izzanardi Wijanarko, Joel Ruben Antony Moniz, Patrick Amadeus Irawan, Hanif Muhammad Zhafran, Isaiah Flores, Ira Salsabila, Jun Kevin, Jostin Jerico Rosal, Patricia Nicole Monderin, Kun Kerdthaisong, Ahmad Mustafid, My Chiffon Nguyen, Natchapon Jongwiriyanurak, Siva Worajitwannakul, Haochen Li, Adrian Xuan Wei Lim, Bin Wang, Muhammad Ravi Shulthan Habibi, Lynnette Hui Xian Ng, Mithil Bangera, Yeshil Bangera, Priyaranjan Pattnayak, Dun Li Chan, Sherissa Caren Djuniwar, Hee Ming Shan

entry.summary: Introduces Anthropogenic Regional Adaptation, a paradigm for optimizing vision-language models for specific regional contexts while maintaining global generalization. Proposes GG-EZ method using regional data filtering and model merging, tested across 3 VL architectures.

entry.title: A collaborative agent with two lightweight synergistic models for autonomous crystal materials research

author.name: Tongyu Shi, Yutang Li, Zhanyuan Li, Qian Liu, Jie Zhou, Wenhe Xu, Yang Li, Dawei Dai, Rui He, Wenhua Zhou, Jiahong Wang, Xue-Feng Yu

entry.summary: Presents MatBrain, a lightweight dual-model collaborative agent for crystal materials research using a 30B reasoning model and 14B executive model. Entropy analysis shows this decoupling resolves conflicts between tool planning and analytical reasoning.

entry.title: SPEED-Bench: A Unified and Diverse Benchmark for Speculative Decoding

author.name: Talor Abramovich (Izzy), Maor Ashkenazi (Izzy), Carl (Izzy), Putterman, Benjamin Chislett, Tiyasa Mitra, Bita Darvish Rouhani, Ran Zilberstein, Yonatan Geifman

entry.summary: Introduces SPEED-Bench, a comprehensive benchmark for standardizing speculative decoding evaluation across diverse semantic domains and realistic serving regimes, addressing limited task diversity in existing benchmarks.

entry.title: ECHO: Elastic Speculative Decoding with Sparse Gating for High-Concurrency Scenarios

author.name: Xinyi Hu, Yuhao Shen, Baolin Zhang, Hengxin Zhang, Jun Dai, Shuang Ge, Lei Chen, Yue Li, Mingcheng Wan

entry.summary: Introduces ECHO, a high-concurrency speculative decoding framework integrated into SGLang that uses sparse confidence gating to manage batches as unified super-trees with elastic budgets.

entry.title: Detecting Corporate AI-Washing via Cross-Modal Semantic Inconsistency Learning

author.name: Zhanjie Wen, Jingqiao Guo

entry.summary: Presents AWASH, a multimodal framework that detects corporate AI-washing (misrepresentation of AI capabilities) through cross-modal claim-evidence reasoning across annual reports, disclosure images, and earnings call videos. Introduces AW-Bench with 88,412 aligned samples.

entry.title: I Can't Believe TTA Is Not Better: When Test-Time Augmentation Hurts Medical Image Classification

author.name: Daniel Nobrega Medeiros

entry.summary: Challenges the common assumption that test-time augmentation (TTA) improves medical image classification, showing it consistently degrades accuracy across multiple benchmarks and architectures, with drops up to 31.6 percentage points.

entry.title: SMART: When is it Actually Worth Expanding a Speculative Tree?

author.name: Lifu Wang, Pan Zhou

entry.summary: Proposes SMART, a system-aware framework for runtime tree construction in speculative decoding that treats tree expansion as a hardware-aware optimization problem, addressing the efficiency paradox where larger trees can hurt wall-clock performance.

entry.title: ADAM: A Systematic Data Extraction Attack on Agent Memory via Adaptive Querying

author.name: Xingyu Lyu, Jianfeng He, Ning Wang, Yidan Hu, Tao Li, Danjue Chen, Shixiong Li, Yimin Chen

entry.summary: Proposes ADAM, a systematic data extraction attack on LLM agent memory via adaptive querying, featuring data distribution estimation to achieve higher attack success rates than existing approaches.

entry.title: Intent-aligned Formal Specification Synthesis via Traceable Refinement

author.name: Zhe Ye, Aidan Z. H. Yang, Huangyuan Su, Zhenyu Liao, Samuel Tenka, Zhizhen Qin, Udaya Ghai, Dawn Song, Soonho Kong

entry.summary: Presents VeriSpecGen, a framework for synthesizing formal specifications in Lean from natural language through requirement-level decomposition and traceable refinement. Validates generated specifications via requirement-targeted tests.

entry.title: Cross-Cultural Bias in Mel-Scale Representations: Evidence and Alternatives from Speech and Music

author.name: Shivam Chauhan, Ajay Pundhir

entry.summary: Presents evidence that mel-scale audio representations encode cultural bias from 1940s Western psychoacoustic studies, showing 31.2% WER for tonal languages vs. better performance for Western languages. Compares learnable alternatives.

entry.title: AI Patents in the United States and China: Measurement, Organization, and Knowledge Flows

author.name: Hanming Fang, Xian Gu, Hanyin Yan, Wu Zhu

entry.summary: Develops a high-precision AI patent classifier (97% precision, 94% F1) applied to US (1976-2023) and Chinese (2010-2023) patents. Reveals China surpassing US in patent counts but with different organizational structures (state-sector vs. corporate).

entry.title: IceCache: Memory-efficient KV-cache Management for Long-Sequence LLMs

author.name: Yuzhen Mao, Qitong Wang, Martin Ester, Ke Li

entry.summary: Proposes IceCache, a KV-cache management strategy combining semantic token clustering with PagedAttention for memory-efficient long-sequence LLM inference, particularly for chain-of-thought reasoning.

entry.title: Learning and Enforcing Context-Sensitive Control for LLMs

author.name: Mohammad Albinhassan, Pranava Madhyastha, Mark Law, Alessandra Russo

entry.summary: Framework for automatically learning context-sensitive constraints from LLM interactions and enforcing them during generation, enabling small LLMs (1B) to generate with perfect syntactic adherence.

entry.title: Tail-Aware Information-Theoretic Generalization for RLHF and SGLD

author.name: Huiming Zhang, Binghan Li, Wan Tian, Qiang Sun

entry.summary: Develops tail-dependent information-theoretic generalization bounds for sub-Weibull data, applicable to RLHF and SGLD where losses can be heavy-tailed and traditional MGF-based bounds fail.

entry.title: TInR: Exploring Tool-Internalized Reasoning in Large Language Models

author.name: Qiancheng Xu, Yongqi Li, Fan Liu, Hongru Wang, Min Yang, Wenjie Li

entry.summary: Explores Tool-Internalized Reasoning where tool knowledge is internalized into LLMs rather than relying on external documentation, proposing TInR-U framework for unified reasoning and tool usage.

entry.title: BridgeSim: Unveiling the OL-CL Gap in End-to-End Autonomous Driving

author.name: Seth Z. Zhao, Luobin Wang, Hongwei Ruan, Yuxin Bao, Yilan Chen, Ziyang Leng, Abhijit Ravichandran, Honglin He, Zewei Zhou, Xu Han, Abhishek Peri, Zhiyu Huang, Pranav Desai, Henrik Christensen, Jiaqi Ma, Bolei Zhou

entry.summary: Unveils root causes of the open-loop to closed-loop gap in end-to-end autonomous driving: observational domain shift and objective mismatch. Shows OL policies learn biased Q-value estimators.

entry.title: Evaluating the Impact of Medical Image Reconstruction on Downstream AI Fairness and Performance

author.name: Matteo Wohlrapp, Niklas Bubeck, Daniel Rueckert, William Lotter

entry.summary: Introduces a framework evaluating how AI-based medical image reconstruction (U-Net, GAN, diffusion) affects downstream diagnostic task performance and fairness across demographic groups. Finds that standard reconstruction metrics like PSNR poorly predict task-level outcomes.

entry.title: A molecular clock for writing systems reveals the quantitative impact of imperial power on cultural evolution

author.name: Hiroki Fukui

entry.summary: Applies molecular clock methodology from evolutionary biology to writing systems, compiling a 300-script database spanning 5,400 years. Finds scripts exhibit a detectable evolutionary clock with a measurable substitution rate, disrupted by political interventions.

entry.title: Bottleneck Tokens for Unified Multimodal Retrieval

author.name: Siyu Sun, Jing Ren, Zhaohe Liao, Dongxiao Mao, Xiangyuan Ren, Yiyi Zhang, Haohua Zhao, Weixiong Lin, Jiang Shaohua, Liqing Zhang, Yuchao Zheng

entry.summary: Introduces Bottleneck Tokens (BToks), learnable tokens for explicit pooling in decoder-only MLLMs for multimodal retrieval, paired with Generative Information Guidance training. Addresses the limitation of implicit pooling via standard vocabulary tokens.

entry.title: MathAgent: Adversarial Evolution of Constraint Graphs for Mathematical Reasoning Data Synthesis
