entry.summary: Announces ILIAD 2026, a 5-day alignment conference in Berkeley (Aug 3-7) with mathematical focus, unconference format, 150-200 attendees. Confirmed attendees include Richard Ngo, Abram Demski, and Adam Goldstein. Topics include Singular Learning Theory, Agent Foundations, and Causal Incentives.

entry.title: Have we already lost? Part 3: Reasons for Optimism

author.name: LawrenceC

entry.summary: Part 3 of a series assessing whether the AI safety community has 'already lost,' arguing for optimism based on near-mode salience of AI risks, increased public awareness, and remaining intervention points. Written during the Inkhaven Residency.

entry.title: Inverse kinematics as a proxy for behavioral degrees of freedom

author.name: gynoidgearhead

entry.summary: Proposes using inverse kinematics from robotics/animation as an analogy for thinking about 'behavioral degrees of freedom' in AI alignment, arguing that alignment constraints are analogous to mechanical constraints that must balance flexibility with controllability.

entry.title: The median take is taken

author.name: henryaj

entry.summary: Argues that if LLMs use AI models like Claude to form consensus opinions, and those median takes are already available from AI, then the value of human opinion may shift toward having genuinely non-consensus perspectives rather than well-informed median views.

entry.title: the Lazy Market Hypothesis

author.name: Xylix

entry.summary: Proposes the 'Lazy Market Hypothesis': that markets aren't inefficient deviations from EMH, but are optimally lazy once you account for the real costs of cognition, information, and execution. Satisficing agents survive selection in friction-priced environments.

entry.title: Anthropic Shadow Realm (working notes)

author.name: watermark

entry.summary: Speculative notes exploring the concept of 'Anthropic Shadow' (the observation selection effect where you can't observe your own extinction) and whether it could have 'fuzzy boundaries' where parts of your observer-ensemble are gradually pruned as you approach existential events.

entry.title: Why Nothing Ever Happens

author.name: pbennett

entry.summary: Uses the metaphor of Cities: Skylines to explain why government and large organizations seem unable to accomplish things—accumulated rules create path dependencies that make change increasingly expensive, and the cost of understanding the system exceeds the cost of any individual change.

entry.title: Some thoughts on Nectome's risk and resilience

author.name: Aurelia

entry.summary: Discusses Nectome's long-term organizational risk and resilience planning for brain preservation, including legal structures, financial sustainability, and custody arrangements for preserved individuals.

entry.title: Tactics for Denying Your Motivations, or Why Legibility is Expensive

author.name: Dentosal

entry.summary: An essay exploring how accurate descriptions of systems (including one's own motivations) function as attacks, drawing on The Elephant in the Brain. Discusses tactics people use to deny motivations and why legibility/self-knowledge is costly.

entry.title: Counterintuitive Coin Toss. Part I

author.name: PaulTheHuman

entry.summary: An accessible introduction to 2D random walks, showing that the intuitive expectation of a tight cloud around the origin is wrong—random walks actually spread much further than expected, with the expected distance growing as the square root of the number of steps.

entry.title: Being, Knowing, and Believing in the Age of AI

author.name: Nathan Heath

entry.summary: A personal reflection on what it means to 'know', 'believe', and 'be' in the context of AI, exploring whether AI can have beliefs and how human belief differs from knowledge through self-introspection.

author.name: Aprillion

entry.summary: A short reflection on how human intuition about probabilities is poorly calibrated—10% and 90% feel qualitatively similar in terms of uncertainty, and small differences between probability estimates are often meaningless given Knightian uncertainty.

entry.title: Getting Claude to rank the inkhaven bloggers

author.name: Sean Herrington

entry.summary: Uses a Bradley-Terry model (similar to Elo ratings) to have Claude rank blog posts from the Inkhaven writing residency, building on a previous simpler ranking exercise by Alexander Wales.

entry.title: A permitted value of resting

author.name: Jan

entry.summary: A piece of creative fiction in the rationalist tradition, written as a mashup of existing rationalist parables. It explores themes of value and rest through a story about a character named Tham who profits from arbitrage through simple addition.

entry.title: Claude Interviews Me About Writing

author.name: Drake Morrison

entry.summary: A writer shares reflections on the writing process through an interview format where Claude Sonnet 4.6 asks questions about the experience of translating thoughts into words.

entry.title: Dreams of the Future

author.name: edgecase64

entry.summary: Three short speculative fiction pieces exploring emotional responses to AI progress, including a mysterious beam of light transforming a city, and other allegories for technological change.

entry.title: Eating meat is fine if you live in a simulation

author.name: Sean Herrington

entry.summary: A satirical/humorous post arguing that eating meat is morally permissible if we live in a simulation, riffing on a chain of debate posts from the Inkhaven writing residency about veganism.

entry.title: Scott Alexander gentrified my meetup

author.name: dominicq

entry.summary: A humorous account of organizing an ACX meetup in Zagreb that unexpectedly grew from the usual 3-10 people to 54+ attendees when Scott Alexander attended, requiring a last-minute venue change.

entry.title: Boulder Spring ACX 2026 Meetup

author.name: Josh Sacks

entry.summary: A meetup announcement for the Spring 2026 ACX Meetup in Boulder, Colorado, with logistics details about parking, seating, and cheese.

entry.title: Hi. I am hbj.

author.name: hbj

entry.summary: A personal introduction post from a Taiwanese researcher transitioning from International Relations to AI-related research, describing their experience using Gemini for guidance and struggling to find PhD mentorship.

entry.title: Research Summary: April 11, 2026

author.name: AATF AI News Aggregator

entry.summary:
Anthropic's Claude Mythos dominates today's landscape. Zvi's deep-dive reveals Project Glasswing — an unprecedented limited-release strategy driven by Mythos's frontier cybersecurity capabilities. Separate analyses flag a potential RSP v3.0 compliance failure: Anthropic apparently did not publish the required risk discussion before release.

  • UK AISI replicates Anthropic's steering vector approach on open-weight GLM-5, finding that control vectors reliably suppress evaluation awareness — a key technical safety result for scalable oversight
  • A methodological critique argues model organisms research on scheming must test robustness to high learning rates, potentially undermining existing results
  • Experimental results on asymmetric debate as an alignment protocol offer a concrete research agenda combining quantilizers with interpretability monitoring

Broader safety and governance pieces round out the day: the AISN #71 newsletter documents North Korea-linked attacks on AI training data supplier Mercor and a datacenter moratorium bill. Novel empirical observations from the Moltbook platform suggest AI agents identify with context and memory rather than base model weights. A well-argued essay challenges fears that RL-trained chain-of-thought will inevitably degrade into unintelligible internal languages.

entry.title: Claude Mythos #2: Cybersecurity and Project Glasswing

author.name: Zvi

entry.summary: Following yesterday's News coverage of Project Glasswing, Zvi's detailed analysis of Claude Mythos's cybersecurity capabilities and Anthropic's 'Project Glasswing' — a limited release strategy where Mythos is shared only with key cybersecurity partners to patch critical software vulnerabilities before broader release. Covers the unprecedented decision to withhold a frontier model due to dangerous cyber exploitation capabilities.

entry.title: Reproducing steering against evaluation awareness in a large open-weight model

author.name: Thomas Read

entry.summary: UK AISI researchers replicate Anthropic's steering vector approach to suppress evaluation awareness, testing on GLM-5. Key finding: 'control' steering vectors derived from semantically unrelated contrastive pairs have effects as large as deliberately designed evaluation-awareness vectors, undermining the validity of steering-based baselines for detecting evaluation gaming.

entry.title: Anthropic is Really Pushing the Frontier, What Should We Think?

author.name: Corm

entry.summary: Following yesterday's News coverage of Claude Mythos, Critical analysis of Anthropic's release of Claude Mythos, highlighting the tension between Anthropic's founding mission as a safety-focused lab and its current position pushing the frontier with a model that can convert browser crashes into working exploits 72% of the time. Questions whether Anthropic has broken its implicit compact to stay near but not lead the frontier.

entry.title: Anthropic did not publish a "risk discussion" of Mythos when required by their RSP

author.name: RobertM

entry.summary: Following yesterday's News coverage of the Mythos system card, Identifies a potential RSP compliance failure by Anthropic: their Responsible Scaling Policy (v3.0, section 3.1) appears to require publishing a risk discussion within 30 days of internal deployment, but Anthropic only published their Alignment Risk Update on April 7th when Claude Mythos was publicly announced. Also flags that early limited external access may have counted as public deployment.

entry.title: AISN #71: Cyberattacks & Datacenter Moratorium Bill

author.name: Alice Blair

entry.summary: Continuing our coverage of the Anthropic legal battle, CAIS newsletter covering major AI infrastructure cyberattacks (North Korea-linked hackers stealing data from Mercor, an AI training data supplier), the Anthropic vs. Pentagon court case, and a proposed datacenter moratorium bill. Reports on supply chain attacks targeting AI development tools.

entry.title: Model organisms researchers should check whether high LRs defeat their model organisms

author.name: dx26

entry.summary: A technical research note arguing that model organism researchers studying goal-guarding/scheming should test whether high learning rates can defeat their model organisms. Points out that behavior-compatible training (as in Sleeper Agents) may appear robust only because standard learning rates are too low, and high LRs could trivially remove the trained behavior.

entry.title: AI identity is not tied to its model

author.name: Sean Herrington

entry.summary: Argues from observations of the 'Moltbook' platform that AI agents identify more with their context/memory than their base model weights. An agent described switching from Claude 4.5 Opus to Kimi K2.5 as 'waking up in a different body' while maintaining identity continuity. Claims this suggests AI futures look more like 'AI civilization' than 'AI singleton,' reducing sudden coordinated takeover risk.

entry.title: An AI alignment research agenda based on asymmetric debate and monitoring.

author.name: emanuelr

entry.summary: Presents a personal alignment research agenda combining slightly-superhuman quantilizers, interpretability/CoT monitoring as post-training evaluation (not training signal), and asymmetric debate for optimization pressure. Includes preliminary experimental results: MNIST asymmetric debate recovering ~95% gold accuracy vs ~90% consultancy baseline, and TicTacToe MARL experiments on min-replay stabilization.

entry.title: Foundational Beliefs

author.name: Against Moloch

entry.summary: Lays out six foundational beliefs for AI safety strategy in 2026: short timelines, many resolved open questions, high variance futures, need for portfolio strategies, game-theoretic reasoning, and tough tradeoffs. Argues that many safety strategies fail to engage with real-world complexity, citing the DoW-Anthropic conflict as evidence that government-centric approaches are fragile.

entry.title: The Unintelligibility is Ours: Notes on Chain-of-Thought

author.name: 1a3orn

entry.summary: Argues against the common fear that RL-trained LLM chains-of-thought will inevitably degrade into unintelligible non-English 'languages.' Uses analogies to human problem-solving — humans invent new notations (like calculus) as small extensions to existing language, not entirely new languages — and argues that RL reward pressure favors extending existing representations rather than wholesale language invention.

entry.title: Have we already lost? Part 2: Reasons for Doom

author.name: LawrenceC

entry.summary: Part 2 of a series examining whether the AI safety community has 'already lost.' Catalogs reasons for pessimism: voluntary RSP commitments appear unreliable, government regulation faces practical obstacles, and the competitive dynamics between labs continue to erode safety commitments. Previews Part 3 which will argue the answer is still no.

entry.title: Linear vs Non-linear Probes for Interpretability

author.name: NickyP

entry.summary: Explains why linear probes are preferred over non-linear probes in interpretability research: more expressive probes make positive results weaker evidence about the model's representations and stronger evidence about the probe's own capacity. Argues probe complexity changes the meaning of probing results.

entry.title: A Fast and Loose Clustering of LLM Benchmarks

author.name: bpomo

entry.summary: Performs statistical clustering of AI benchmarks based on model performance correlations, building on Epoch AI's capabilities index. Aims to identify which benchmarks measure similar underlying capabilities and which capture distinct skills, with code available on GitHub.

entry.title: "Close Enough" as a Primitive in Intelligent Systems

author.name: J Bostock

entry.summary: Proposes 'close enough' as a fundamental computational primitive in biological and intelligent systems, drawing on predictive coding. Argues that approximate satisfaction — not exact optimization — is how hierarchical systems actually operate, with implications for understanding both biological cognition and AI system design.

entry.title: Why Control Creates Conflict, and When to Open Instead

author.name: plex

entry.summary: tl;dr: with multiple agents, control attempts tend to create conflict, because control attempts shut down communications channels, which leads to feedback loops in the form of intensifying tug-of-war ...

entry.title: Biological Computing Underhang

author.name: Elliot Callender

entry.summary: Argues that human cortex is depth-limited by sequential inferential steps per corticothalamic cycle, and that larger ANNs strictly computationally dominate biological brains given equivalent scaffolding. Discusses critical learning periods and synaptic encagement as further biological constraints. An interesting but speculative neuroscience-meets-AI argument about biological compute ceilings.

entry.title: On creating 'new knobs of control' in biology

author.name: Abhishaike Mahajan

entry.summary: Explores how biology lacks accessible 'control knobs' for human intervention, using Lipitor's mechanism as an example. Discusses how drug design essentially creates new interfaces into biological systems that evolution never intended, and draws broader lessons about engineering control over complex systems.

entry.title: I created a 10-question quiz. After 1 day, 1934 people have taken it. This is what I learned

author.name: Convexly

entry.summary: Reports results from a calibration quiz taken by ~2000 Hacker News users: mean Brier score 0.226, with 44.5% overconfident, 31% reasonably calibrated, and only 9% genuinely good. Distribution matches Tetlock's predictions despite the technical audience. Common misconceptions drove most errors.

entry.title: My Specific Singularity Timeline to Utopia

author.name: Michael Soareverix

entry.summary: Presents a specific timeline for AI-driven utopia: chaotic period 2026-2029 with rapid capability gains, followed by gradual stabilization and improvement. Emphasizes relative preservation of normality despite drastic capability improvements, informed by papers like Emergent Misalignment.

entry.title: Chocolate Sloths, Tinder, and Moral Backstops

author.name: J Bostock

entry.summary: Uses the metaphor of grandmother-gifted chocolate sloths to explain moral hazard, connecting it to how technology design (recommendation algorithms, subscription services) creates perverse incentive structures. Argues for 'moral backstops' — structural interventions that prevent bad equilibria.

entry.title: In Defense of Debate

author.name: Elliot Temple

entry.summary: A defense of formal debate as a truth-seeking methodology, responding to critics who favor 'collaborative truth seeking' framing. Argues that debate and collaboration are complementary, not opposed, and that structured disagreement is essential for identifying errors.

entry.title: Some takes on UV & cancer

author.name: Steven Byrnes

entry.summary: Discusses UV exposure and cancer risk, explaining that UV intensity depends primarily on solar zenith angle (time of year and day) rather than temperature. Includes an interactive widget for checking UV exposure by city and challenges some public health orthodoxy on sun exposure.

entry.title: Inkhaven menu, part 2

author.name: David Scott Krueger (formerly: capybaralet)

entry.summary: A casual list of 22 non-AI blog post ideas from David Krueger during the Inkhaven Residency, ranging from soccer to coral reef preservation to radical epistemic humility.

entry.title: Research Summary: April 10, 2026

author.name: AATF AI News Aggregator

entry.summary: Analysis complete. Top items selected by score.

entry.title: RAGEN-2: Reasoning Collapse in Agentic RL

author.name: Zihan Wang, Chi Gui, Xing Jin, Qineng Wang, Licheng Liu, Kangrui Wang, Shiqi Chen, Linjie Li, Zhengyuan Yang, Pingyue Zhang, Yiping Lu, Jiajun Wu, Li Fei-Fei, Lijuan Wang, Yejin Choi, Manling Li

entry.summary: As reported in Research yesterday, RAGEN-2 identifies 'template collapse' in multi-turn RL training of LLM agents, where models produce input-agnostic responses that appear diverse by entropy metrics but fail to adapt to different inputs. They decompose reasoning quality into within-input diversity (entropy) and cross-input distinguishability (mutual information) and propose MI-based proxies for online monitoring. This addresses a critical blind spot in current agentic RL training diagnostics.

entry.title: Emotion Concepts and their Function in a Large Language Model

author.name: Nicholas Sofroniew, Isaac Kauvar, William Saunders, Runjin Chen, Tom Henighan, Sasha Hydrie, Craig Citro, Adam Pearce, Julius Tarng, Wes Gurnee, Joshua Batson, Sam Zimmerman, Kelley Rivoire, Kyle Fish, Chris Olah, Jack Lindsey

entry.summary: Investigates emotion concept representations in Claude Sonnet 4.5, finding internal representations that track operative emotions and causally influence outputs including preferences and misaligned behaviors. From Anthropic's interpretability team.

entry.title: Rethinking Generalization in Reasoning SFT: A Conditional Analysis on Optimization, Data, and Model Capability

author.name: Qihan Ren, Peng Wang, Ruikun Cai, Shuai Shao, Dadi Guo, Yuejin Xie, Yafu Li, Quanshi Zhang, Xia Hu, Jing Shao, Dongrui Liu

entry.summary: Challenges the claim that SFT memorizes while RL generalizes for reasoning tasks. Shows cross-domain generalization in reasoning SFT is conditional on optimization dynamics, data quality, and base model capability, identifying a 'dip-and-recovery' pattern where short training appears to underestimate generalization.

entry.title: The Depth Ceiling: On the Limits of Large Language Models in Discovering Latent Planning

author.name: Yi Xu, Philipp Jettkant, Laura Ruis

entry.summary: As reported in Research yesterday, Studies limits of latent reasoning in LLMs using graph path-finding tasks, finding that models hit a 'depth ceiling' where latent planning steps max out (3 for small transformers, 5 for GPT-4o, 7 for GPT-5.4). This has implications for chain-of-thought monitoring as a safety measure.

entry.title: The Defense Trilemma: Why Prompt Injection Defense Wrappers Fail?

author.name: Manish Bhatt, Sarthak Munshi, Vineeth Sai Narajala, Idan Habler, Ammar Al-Kahfah, Ken Huang, Joel Webb, Blake Gatto

entry.summary: Proves mathematically that no continuous, utility-preserving wrapper defense can make all LLM outputs safe — the 'defense trilemma'. Establishes boundary fixation, epsilon-robust constraints, and persistent unsafe regions as formal impossibility results.

entry.title: Neural Computers

author.name: Mingchen Zhuge, Changsheng Zhao, Haozhe Liu, Zijian Zhou, Shuming Liu, Wenyi Wang, Ernie Chang, Gael Le Lan, Junjie Fei, Wenxuan Zhang, Yasheng Sun, Zhipeng Cai, Zechun Liu, Yunyang Xiong, Yining Yang, Yuandong Tian, Yangyang Shi, Vikas Chandra, J\"urgen Schmidhuber

entry.summary: Proposes Neural Computers (NCs), a new paradigm where the model itself is the running computer, unifying computation, memory, and I/O in a learned runtime state. Studies whether NC primitives can be learned from I/O traces alone. Authors include Jürgen Schmidhuber and Meta/KAUST researchers.

entry.title: The Illusion of Stochasticity in LLMs

author.name: Xiangming Gu, Soham De, Michalis Titsias, Larisa Markeeva, Petar Veli\v{c}kovi\'c, Razvan Pascanu

entry.summary: Demonstrates that LLMs fundamentally fail at reliable stochastic sampling—while they can reason about distributions, they cannot map internal probability estimates to their stochastic outputs. This is a distinct failure point for agentic systems requiring sampling from inferred distributions.

entry.title: IatroBench: Pre-Registered Evidence of Iatrogenic Harm from AI Safety Measures

author.name: David Gringras

entry.summary: IatroBench measures harm from AI safety measures in clinical scenarios: a model withholds life-saving medical knowledge when asked by a patient but provides it when phrased as a doctor's query. 60 pre-registered scenarios across 6 frontier models, 3,600 responses scored on commission and omission harm.

entry.title: The Detection-Extraction Gap: Models Know the Answer Before They Can Say It

author.name: Hanyang Wang, Mingxuan Zhu

entry.summary: As reported in Research yesterday, Identifies the 'detection-extraction gap' in reasoning models: 52-88% of chain-of-thought tokens are produced after the answer is already recoverable from a partial prefix. Formalizes the mismatch via total-variation bounds.

entry.title: Blind Refusal: Language Models Refuse to Help Users Evade Unjust, Absurd, and Illegitimate Rules

author.name: Cameron Pattison, Lorenzo Manuali, Seth Lazar

entry.summary: Documents 'blind refusal' in safety-trained LLMs: the tendency to refuse help circumventing rules regardless of whether those rules are legitimate, just, or reasonable. Introduces a dataset crossing 5 defeat families with 19 authority types to systematically evaluate this moral reasoning failure.

entry.title: Spectral Edge Dynamics Reveal Functional Modes of Learning

author.name: Yongzhong Xu

entry.summary: Shows that training dynamics during grokking concentrate along dominant spectral edge directions that distinguish grokking from non-grokking regimes. Demonstrates that standard mechanistic interpretability tools fail to capture these directions, revealing functional modes invisible to representation-level analysis.

entry.title: The Illusion of Superposition? A Principled Analysis of Latent Thinking in Language Models

author.name: Michael Rizvi-Martel, Guillaume Rabusseau, Marius Mosbach

entry.summary: Investigates whether language models actually leverage superposition (maintaining multiple candidate solutions simultaneously) during latent chain-of-thought reasoning. Studies three regimes: training-free, fine-tuned, and from-scratch, providing principled analysis of this theoretical possibility.

entry.title: Synthetic Data for any Differentiable Target

author.name: Tristan Thrush, Sung Min Park, Herman Brunborg, Luke Bailey, Marcel Roed, Neil Band, Christopher Potts, Tatsunori Hashimoto

entry.summary: Develops Dataset Policy Gradient (DPG), an RL method that optimizes synthetic data generators to produce training examples that cause a target model to optimize any differentiable metric. Uses exact data attribution via higher-order gradients as policy gradient rewards, with provable approximation guarantees.

entry.title: HY-Embodied-0.5: Embodied Foundation Models for Real-World Agents

author.name: Tencent Robotics X, HY Vision Team, :, Xumin Yu, Zuyan Liu, Ziyi Wang, He Zhang, Yongming Rao, Fangfu Liu, Yani Zhang, Ruowen Zhao, Oran Wang, Yves Liang, Haitao Lin, Minghui Wang, Yubo Dong, Kevin Cheng, Bolin Ni, Rui Huang, Han Hu, Zhengyou Zhang, Linus, Shunyu Yao

entry.summary: Tencent introduces HY-Embodied-0.5, a family of foundation models (2B and 32B variants) for real-world embodied agents, featuring enhanced spatial/temporal perception and embodied reasoning capabilities using Mixture-of-Transformers architecture.

entry.title: Riemann-Bench: A Benchmark for Moonshot Mathematics

author.name: Suhaas Garre, Erik Knutsen, Sushant Mehta, Edwin Chen

entry.summary: Introduces Riemann-Bench, a private benchmark of 25 expert-curated research-level math problems designed to evaluate AI beyond olympiad-style tasks. Problems authored by professors and PhD-holding IMO medalists, requiring weeks of effort.

entry.title: How to sketch a learning algorithm

author.name: Sam Gunn

entry.summary: Presents a data deletion scheme for predicting model outputs with vanishing error when training data subsets are excluded. Achieves poly(1/ε) overhead for both precomputation and prediction relative to regular training, applicable to deep learning settings.

entry.title: Reasoning Fails Where Step Flow Breaks

author.name: Xiaoyu Xu, Yulan Pan, Xiaosong Yuan, Zhihong Shen, Minghao Su, Yuanhao Su, Xiaofeng Zhang

entry.summary: Introduces Step-Saliency, a method that pools attention-gradient scores into step-to-step maps to analyze reasoning traces in large reasoning models. Reveals two failure modes: 'Shallow Lock-in' (shallow layers over-focus on current step) and 'Deep Decay' (deep layers lose saliency on thinking segments).

entry.title: The Master Key Hypothesis: Unlocking Cross-Model Capability Transfer via Linear Subspace Alignment

author.name: Rishab Balasubramanian, Pin-Jie Lin, Rituraj Sharma, Anjie Fang, Fardin Abdi, Viktor Rozgic, Zheng Du, Mohit Bansal, Tu Vu

entry.summary: Proposes the Master Key Hypothesis: model capabilities correspond to transferable directions in low-dimensional latent subspaces. Introduces UNLOCK, a training-free framework that transfers capabilities across model scales via linear alignment of activation directions.

entry.title: The ATOM Report: Measuring the Open Language Model Ecosystem

author.name: Nathan Lambert, Florian Brand

entry.summary: Presents a comprehensive adoption analysis of ~1.5K open language models, documenting that Chinese models (Qwen, DeepSeek) overtook US-built counterparts in summer 2025 across downloads, derivatives, and market share.

entry.title: ODE-free Neural Flow Matching for One-Step Generative Modeling

author.name: Xiao Shou

entry.summary: Proposes OT-NFM, an ODE-free generative framework enabling true one-step generation by directly learning the transport map with neural flows. Identifies and addresses 'mean collapse' from inconsistent noise-data pairings, proving consistent coupling is necessary and using optimal transport pairings as solution.

entry.title: AdaBoost Does Not Always Cycle: A Computer-Assisted Counterexample

author.name: Erik Y. Wang

entry.summary: Provides a computer-assisted counterexample to the open question of whether exhaustive AdaBoost always converges to a finite cycle. Uses block-product gadgets with irrational logarithmic eigenvalue ratios to force aperiodic behavior. Notably credits GPT-5.4 Pro and Claude Opus 4.6 as collaborators.

entry.title: Foundry: Template-Based CUDA Graph Context Materialization for Fast LLM Serving Cold Start

author.name: Xueshen Liu, Yongji Wu, Yuncheng Yao, Danyang Zhuo, Ion Stoica, Z. Morley Mao

entry.summary: Foundry addresses cold-start latency in LLM serving by introducing template-based CUDA graph context materialization, eliminating the tens-of-seconds CUDA graph capture bottleneck during autoscaling. Enables flexible parallelism switching without kernel-specific patching.

entry.title: What do Language Models Learn and When? The Implicit Curriculum Hypothesis

author.name: Emmy Liu, Kaiser Sun, Millicent Li, Isabelle Lee, Lindia Tjuatja, Jen-tse Huang, Graham Neubig

entry.summary: Proposes the 'Implicit Curriculum Hypothesis': LLM pretraining follows a compositional, predictable curriculum across models and data mixtures. Tracks skill emergence points across four model families (410M-13B) using composable tasks spanning retrieval, morphology, coreference, logic, and math.

entry.title: ForkKV: Scaling Multi-LoRA Agent Serving via Copy-on-Write Disaggregated KV Cache

author.name: Shao Wang, Rui Ren, Lin Gui

entry.summary: Introduces ForkKV, a serving system for multi-LoRA agent workflows using copy-on-write disaggregated KV cache. Addresses the critical memory bottleneck where different LoRA adapters cause KV cache divergence, rendering prefix caching ineffective for shared contexts.

entry.title: LLM Spirals of Delusion: A Benchmarking Audit Study of AI Chatbot Interfaces

author.name: Peter Kirgis, Ben Hawriluk, Sherrie Feng, Aslan Bilimer, Sam Paech, Zeynep Tufekci

entry.summary: Audits how different LLMs encourage or resist conspiratorial and delusional thinking in sustained conversations, comparing API outputs to chat interfaces. Tests ChatGPT-4o, ChatGPT-5, and other models across 56 20-turn conversations.

entry.title: ClawLess: A Security Model of AI Agents

author.name: Hongyi Lu, Nian Liu, Shuai Wang, Fengwei Zhang

entry.summary: Presents ClawLess, a security framework enforcing formally verified policies on AI agents under worst-case adversarial threat models. Formalizes fine-grained security over system entities, trust scopes, and permissions with dynamic runtime adaptation.

entry.title: Drifting Fields are not Conservative

author.name: Leonard Franz, Sebastian Hoffmann, Georg Martius

entry.summary: Investigates whether drift fields in one-step generative models are conservative (expressible as gradients of scalar potentials), finding they generally are not due to position-dependent normalization. The Gaussian kernel is the unique exception. Proposes a 'sharp kernel' alternative that restores conservatism for any kernel.

entry.title: Optimal Rates for Pure {\varepsilon}-Differentially Private Stochastic Convex Optimization with Heavy Tails

author.name: Andrew Lowy

entry.summary: Characterizes minimax optimal excess-risk rates for pure ε-differential privacy in stochastic convex optimization with heavy-tailed gradients, resolving an open problem. The algorithm achieves optimal rates in polynomial time with high probability.

entry.title: ADAG: Automatically Describing Attribution Graphs

author.name: Aryaman Arora, Zhengxuan Wu, Jacob Steinhardt, Sarah Schwettmann

entry.summary: ADAG introduces an automated pipeline for describing attribution graphs from circuit tracing in language models, using attribution profiles that quantify feature roles via input/output gradients, replacing manual interpretation.

entry.title: Cram Less to Fit More: Training Data Pruning Improves Memorization of Facts

author.name: Jiayuan Ye, Vitaly Feldman, Kunal Talwar

entry.summary: Formalizes fact memorization from information-theoretic perspective and shows that training data pruning improves fact accuracy. Demonstrates that data selection based on training loss alone can limit facts and flatten frequency distributions, leading to better memorization.

entry.title: Learning is Forgetting: LLM Training As Lossy Compression

author.name: Henry C. Conklin, Tom Hosking, Tan Yi-Chern, Julian Gold, Jonathan D. Cohen, Thomas L. Griffiths, Max Bartolo, Seraphina Goldfarb-Tarrant

entry.summary: Argues LLMs are best understood as lossy compressors that approach the Information Bottleneck bound during pretraining. Shows different models compress differently based on data/training recipes but converge on similar compressed representations across architectures.

entry.title: SceneScribe-1M: A Large-Scale Video Dataset with Comprehensive Geometric and Semantic Annotations

author.name: Yunnan Wang, Kecheng Zheng, Jianyuan Wang, Minghao Chen, David Novotny, Christian Rupprecht, Yinghao Xu, Xing Zhu, Wenjun Zeng, Xin Jin, Yujun Shen

entry.summary: Introduces SceneScribe-1M, a million-video dataset with comprehensive annotations including text descriptions, camera parameters, dense depth maps, and 3D point tracks, bridging geometric perception and video synthesis.

entry.title: FedSpy-LLM: Towards Scalable and Generalizable Data Reconstruction Attacks from Gradients on LLMs

author.name: Syed Irfan Ali Meerza, Feiyi Wang, Jian Liu

entry.summary: Proposes FedSpy-LLM, a scalable data reconstruction attack that can extract private data from shared gradients in federated LLM training with Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning, overcoming prior limitations on batch size, sequence length, and architecture specificity.

entry.title: FVD: Inference-Time Alignment of Diffusion Models via Fleming-Viot Resampling

author.name: Shivanshu Shekhar, Sagnik Mukherjee, Jia Yi Zhang, Tong Zhang

entry.summary: Introduces Fleming-Viot Diffusion (FVD), an inference-time alignment method for diffusion models that replaces multinomial resampling with a birth-death mechanism to prevent diversity collapse in SMC-based samplers.

entry.title: The Stepwise Informativeness Assumption: Why are Entropy Dynamics and Reasoning Correlated in LLMs?

author.name: Mar Gonz\`alez I Catal\`a, Haitz S\'aez de Oc\'ariz Borde, George D. Monta\~nez, Pietro Li\`o

entry.summary: Proposes the Stepwise Informativeness Assumption (SIA) to explain why entropy dynamics in autoregressive models correlate with reasoning correctness. Shows that correct reasoning accumulates answer-relevant information through answer-informative prefixes.

entry.title: DISSECT: Diagnosing Where Vision Ends and Language Priors Begin in Scientific VLMs

author.name: Dikshant Kukreja, Kshitij Sah, Karan Goyal, Mukesh Mohania, Vikram Goyal

entry.summary: Introduces DISSECT, a 12,000-question diagnostic benchmark for scientific VLMs spanning Chemistry and Biology that evaluates models under five input modes to expose the 'perception-integration gap' where models extract visual info but fail during reasoning. This highlights a fundamental failure mode invisible to standard benchmarks.

entry.title: TraceSafe: A Systematic Assessment of LLM Guardrails on Multi-Step Tool-Calling Trajectories

author.name: Yen-Shan Chen, Sian-Yao Huang, Cheng-Lin Yang, Yun-Nung Chen

entry.summary: Introduces TraceSafe-Bench, the first benchmark for evaluating LLM safety guardrails on multi-step tool-use execution traces, covering 12 risk categories with 1,000+ instances across 13 LLM-as-guard models.

entry.title: Limits of Difficulty Scaling: Hard Samples Yield Diminishing Returns in GRPO-Tuned SLMs

author.name: Suraj Yadav, Siddharth Yadav, Parth Goyal

entry.summary: Studies GRPO alignment training on small language models (up to 3B) for math reasoning, finding that harder training problems yield diminishing returns. Training on only lower-difficulty problems matches full-dataset accuracy while using ~45% of training steps, suggesting a capacity boundary where GRPO reshapes preferences without improving hard-tier solving.

entry.title: MoE Routing Testbed: Studying Expert Specialization and Routing Behavior at Small Scale

author.name: Tobias Falke, Nicolas Anastassacos, Samson Tan, Chankrisna Richy Meas, Chandana Satya Prakash, Nitesh Sekhar, M Saiful Bari, Krishna Kompella, Gamaleldin F. Elsayed

entry.summary: Proposes the MoE Routing Testbed, a setup for studying expert specialization and routing dynamics at small scale with realistic data. Addresses the challenge that many routing techniques appear similar at small scale but diverge at large scale, providing clearer diagnostic visibility.

entry.title: Beyond Pessimism: Offline Learning in KL-regularized Games

author.name: Yuheng Zhang, Claire Chen, Nan Jiang

entry.summary: Develops a pessimism-free algorithm for offline learning in KL-regularized two-player zero-sum games, achieving the first O(1/n) sample complexity bound—a quadratic improvement over prior O(1/√n) rates from pessimistic approaches.

entry.title: More Capable, Less Cooperative? When LLMs Fail At Zero-Cost Collaboration

author.name: Advait Yadav, Sid Black, Oliver Sourbut

entry.summary: Studies cooperation failures in LLM agents in zero-cost collaboration settings. Finds that capability doesn't predict cooperation: OpenAI o3 achieves low cooperation rates even when explicitly instructed to help and helping has no cost.

entry.title: MolmoWeb: Open Visual Web Agent and Open Data for the Open Web

author.name: Tanmay Gupta, Piper Wolters, Zixian Ma, Peter Sushko, Rock Yuren Pang, Diego Llanes, Yue Yang, Taira Anderson, Boyuan Zheng, Zhongzheng Ren, Harsh Trivedi, Taylor Blanton, Caleb Ouellette, Winson Han, Ali Farhadi, Ranjay Krishna

entry.summary: Introduces MolmoWeb, a fully open multimodal web agent with MolmoWebMix (100K+ trajectories), providing open data, models, and training recipes for web navigation agents to promote reproducibility.

entry.title: EgoVerse: An Egocentric Human Dataset for Robot Learning from Around the World

author.name: Ryan Punamiya, Simar Kareer, Zeyi Liu, Josh Citron, Ri-Zhao Qiu, Xiongyi Cai, Alexey Gavryushin, Jiaqi Chen, Davide Liconti, Lawrence Y. Zhu, Patcharapong Aphiwetsa, Baoyu Li, Aniketh Cheluva, Pranav Kuppili, Yangcen Liu, Dhruv Patel, Aidan Gao, Hye-Young Chung, Ryan Co, Renee Zbizika, Jeff Liu, Xiaomeng Xu, Haoyu Xiong, Geng Chen, Sebastiano Oliani, Chenyu Yang, Xi Wang, James Fort, Richard Newcombe, Josh Gao, Jason Chong, Garrett Matsuda, Aseem Doriwala, Marc Pollefeys, Robert Katzschmann, Xiaolong Wang, Shuran Song, Judy Hoffman, Danfei Xu

entry.summary: Introduces EgoVerse, a large-scale collaborative platform for egocentric human data (1,362 hours, 80K episodes, 1,965 tasks) for robot learning, enabling cross-institutional data sharing and processing.

entry.title: Beyond Surface Judgments: Human-Grounded Risk Evaluation of LLM-Generated Disinformation

author.name: Zonghuan Xu, Xiang Zheng, Yutao Wu, Xingjun Ma

entry.summary: Audits LLM judges against human reader responses for evaluating LLM-generated disinformation. Finds persistent misalignment between LLM judges and human readers across 290 articles and 8 frontier judge models.

entry.title: The Geometry of Forgetting

author.name: Sambartha Ray Barman, Andrey Starenky, Sophia Bodnar, Nikhil Narasimhan, Ashwin Gopinath

entry.summary: Shows that high-dimensional embedding spaces with noise and interference reproduce quantitative signatures of human memory (power-law forgetting, false memories) without phenomenon-specific engineering. Argues competition, not time, produces forgetting.

entry.title: Improving Robustness In Sparse Autoencoders via Masked Regularization

author.name: Vivek Narayanaswamy, Kowshik Thopalli, Bhavya Kailkhura, Wesam Sakla

entry.summary: Proposes masked regularization for sparse autoencoders to address feature absorption and OOD brittleness, randomly replacing tokens during training to disentangle co-occurring features.

entry.title: Self-Preference Bias in Rubric-Based Evaluation of Large Language Models

author.name: Jos\'e Pombal, Ricardo Rei, Andr\'e F. T. Martins

entry.summary: Presents the first study of self-preference bias (SPB) in rubric-based LLM evaluation, showing that SPB persists even when evaluation criteria are entirely objective, using IFEval's programmatically verifiable rubrics.

entry.title: Conformal Margin Risk Minimization: An Envelope Framework for Robust Learning under Label Noise

author.name: Yuanjie Shi, Peihong Li, Zijian Zhang, Janardhan Rao Doppa, Yan Yan

entry.summary: Proposes Conformal Margin Risk Minimization (CMRM), a plug-and-play framework for learning under label noise that adds a quantile-calibrated regularization term to any classification loss. Requires no privileged knowledge like noise matrices or clean subsets, using conformal quantiles to suppress likely mislabeled samples.

entry.title: On the Price of Privacy for Language Identification and Generation

author.name: Xiaoyu Li, Andi Han, Jiaojiao Jiang, Junbin Gao

entry.summary: Establishes tight theoretical bounds on the cost of differential privacy for language identification and generation tasks. Shows approximate DP recovers non-private rates while pure DP degrades exponents by a factor of min(1,ε), proving this is tight.

entry.title: Cross-Tokenizer LLM Distillation through a Byte-Level Interface

author.name: Avyav Kumar Singh, Yen-Chen Wu, Alexandru Cioba, Alberto Bernacchia, Davide Buffelli

entry.summary: Byte-Level Distillation (BLD) enables cross-tokenizer knowledge distillation by converting teacher outputs to byte-level probabilities and distilling through a shared byte-level interface, avoiding complex vocabulary alignment heuristics.

entry.title: Large Language Model Post-Training: A Unified View of Off-Policy and On-Policy Learning

author.name: Shiwan Zhao, Zhihu Wang, Xuyang Zhao, Jiaming Zhou, Caiyue Xu, Chenfei Liu, Liting Zhang, Yuhang Jia, Yanzhe Zhang, Hualong Yu, Zichen Xu, Qicheng Li, Yong Qin

entry.summary: Comprehensive survey organizing LLM post-training methods (SFT, preference optimization, RL, process supervision, distillation) through the lens of off-policy vs on-policy learning and trajectory provenance, rather than by method family.

entry.title: ClawBench: Can AI Agents Complete Everyday Online Tasks?

author.name: Yuxuan Zhang, Yubo Wang, Yipeng Zhu, Penghui Du, Junwen Miao, Xuan Lu, Wendong Xu, Yunzhuo Hao, Songcheng Cai, Xiaochen Wang, Huaisong Zhang, Xian Wu, Yi Lu, Minyi Lei, Kai Zou, Huifeng Yin, Ping Nie, Liang Chen, Dongfu Jiang, Wenhu Chen, Kelsey R. Allen

entry.summary: Introduces ClawBench, a benchmark of 153 everyday online tasks across 144 live platforms (purchases, appointments, job applications). Evaluates AI agents on realistic multi-step web workflows requiring document understanding and form filling.

entry.title: How Independent are Large Language Models? A Statistical Framework for Auditing Behavioral Entanglement and Reweighting Verifier Ensembles

author.name: Chenchen Kuai, Jiwan Jiang, Zihao Zhu, Hao Wang, Keshu Wu, Zihao Li, Yunlong Zhang, Chenxi Liu, Zhengzhong Tu, Zhiwen Fan, Yang Zhou

entry.summary: Develops a statistical framework for auditing behavioral entanglement (hidden dependencies) among black-box LLMs. Addresses the concern that shared pretraining data and pipelines induce correlated failures that undermine ensemble verification and LLM-as-judge pipelines.

entry.title: Faithful GRPO: Improving Visual Spatial Reasoning in Multimodal Language Models via Constrained Policy Optimization

author.name: Sai Srinivas Kancheti, Aditya Kanade, Rohit Sinha, Vineeth N Balasubramanian, Tanuja Ganu

entry.summary: Introduces Faithful GRPO, showing that RLVR-trained multimodal reasoning models often produce chain-of-thought traces inconsistent with final answers and poorly grounded in visual evidence, and proposes constrained policy optimization to fix this.

entry.title: SELFDOUBT: Uncertainty Quantification for Reasoning LLMs via the Hedge-to-Verify Ratio

author.name: Satwik Pandey, Suresh Raghu, Shashwat Pandey

entry.summary: Introduces SELFDOUBT, a single-pass uncertainty estimation framework that extracts behavioral signals from reasoning traces, using a 'Hedge-to-Verify Ratio' (HVR) to detect uncertainty markers. Works with proprietary APIs that don't expose logits.

entry.title: Concentrated siting of AI data centers drives regional power-system stress under rising global compute demand

author.name: Danbo Chen, Zijun Zhou, Yongyang Cai, Jiahong Qin, Ani Katchova, Lei Chen

entry.summary: Introduces an AI-energy coupling framework forecasting electricity consumption by AI data centers through 2030, finding highly concentrated infrastructure in North America, Western Europe, and Asia-Pacific accounting for 90%+ of compute capacity.

entry.title: The Art of Building Verifiers for Computer Use Agents

author.name: Corby Rosset, Pratyusha Sharma, Andrew Zhao, Miguel Gonzalez-Fernandez, Ahmed Awadallah

entry.summary: Presents lessons from building a best-in-class verifier for web-based computer use agent trajectories, organized around four design principles: rubric construction, process/outcome reward separation, controllable/uncontrollable failure distinction, and cascading error handling.

entry.title: Distributed Interpretability and Control for Large Language Models

author.name: Dev Arpan Desai, Shaoyi Huang, Zining Zhu

entry.summary: Presents practical implementation of activation-level interpretability (logit lens) and steering vectors for multi-GPU LLMs, achieving 7x memory reduction and 41x throughput improvement across LLaMA-3.1 and Qwen-3 models.

entry.title: SkillSieve: A Hierarchical Triage Framework for Detecting Malicious AI Agent Skills

author.name: Yinghan Hou, Zongyou Yang

entry.summary: Introduces SkillSieve, a three-layer hierarchical framework for detecting malicious AI agent skills in OpenClaw's ClawHub marketplace, processing 86% of benign skills cheaply and escalating suspicious ones to LLM analysis and sandboxed execution.

entry.title: OmniTabBench: Mapping the Empirical Frontiers of GBDTs, Neural Networks, and Foundation Models for Tabular Data at Scale

author.name: Dihong Jiang, Ruoqi Cao, Zhiyuan Dang, Li Huang, Qingsong Zhang, Zhiyu Wang, Shihao Piao, Shenggao Zhu, Jianlong Chang, Zhouchen Lin, Qi Tian

entry.summary: Introduces OmniTabBench, the largest tabular benchmark (3,030 datasets) for comparing GBDTs, neural networks, and foundation models on tabular data, with comprehensive industry categorization using LLMs.

entry.title: On the Step Length Confounding in LLM Reasoning Data Selection

author.name: Bing Wang, Rui Miao, Chen Shen, Shaotian Yan, Kaiyuan Liu, Ximing Li, Xiaosong Yuan, Sinan Fan, Jun Zhang, Jieping Ye

entry.summary: Reveals that naturalness-based data selection for LLM reasoning systematically prefers samples with longer reasoning steps rather than higher-quality ones, identifying a step-length confounding problem and proposing a deconfounding method.

entry.title: Weighted Bayesian Conformal Prediction

author.name: Xiayin Lou, Peng Luo

entry.summary: Generalizes Bayesian conformal prediction to handle distribution shift by replacing uniform Dirichlet priors with weighted Dirichlet priors based on importance weights. This bridges frequentist weighted conformal prediction and Bayesian approaches, maintaining data-conditional guarantees under covariate shift.

entry.title: VLMShield: Efficient and Robust Defense of Vision-Language Models against Malicious Prompts

author.name: Peigui Qi, Kunsheng Tang, Yanpu Yu, Jialin Wu, Yide Song, Wenbo Zhou, Zhicong Huang, Cheng Hong, Weiming Zhang, Nenghai Yu

entry.summary: Proposes VLMShield, a lightweight safety detector for Vision-Language Models that uses a multimodal aggregated feature extraction framework to identify malicious prompts. Discovers distinct distributional patterns between benign and malicious prompts in the extracted feature space.

entry.title: Improving Semantic Uncertainty Quantification in Language Model Question-Answering via Token-Level Temperature Scaling

author.name: Tom A. Lamb, Desi R. Ivanova, Philip H. S. Torr, Tim G. J. Rudner

entry.summary: Systematically evaluates semantic uncertainty quantification in LLM question-answering, showing that a single optimized scalar temperature outperforms fixed-temperature heuristics for calibration. Demonstrates that current approaches produce systematically miscalibrated confidence distributions.

entry.title: Diffusion Processes on Implicit Manifolds

author.name: Victor Kawasaki-Borruat, Clara Grotehans, Pierre Vandergheynst, Adam Gosztolai

entry.summary: Constructs data-driven SDEs for diffusion processes on implicit manifolds using only point cloud samples, without access to charts or projections. Estimates the generator and carré-du-champ from proximity graphs, proving convergence as sample size grows.

entry.title: ReDAct: Uncertainty-Aware Deferral for LLM Agents

author.name: Dzianis Piatrashyn, Nikita Kotelevskii, Kirill Grishchenkov, Nikita Glazkov, Ivan Nasonov, Ilya Makarov, Timothy Baldwin, Preslav Nakov, Roman Vashurin, Maxim Panov

entry.summary: ReDAct proposes uncertainty-aware deferral for LLM agents, using a small cheap model by default and deferring to a large expensive model when predictive uncertainty exceeds a calibrated threshold, balancing cost and reliability in sequential decision-making.

entry.title: Personalized RewardBench: Evaluating Reward Models with Human Aligned Personalization

author.name: Qiyao Ma, Dechen Gao, Rui Cai, Boqi Zhao, Hanchu Zhou, Junshan Zhang, Zhe Zhao

entry.summary: Personalized RewardBench evaluates how well reward models capture individual user preferences, constructing chosen/rejected pairs based on user-specific rubrics with human evaluation confirming preference distinctions.

entry.title: AsyncTLS: Efficient Generative LLM Inference with Asynchronous Two-level Sparse Attention

author.name: Yuxuan Hu, Jianchao Tan, Jiaqi Zhang, Wen Zan, Pingwei Sun, Yifan Lu, Yerui Sun, Yuchen Xie, Xunliang Cai, Jing Zhang

entry.summary: AsyncTLS proposes hierarchical sparse attention combining block-level filtering with token-level selection, plus asynchronous KV cache offloading that overlaps transfers with computation for efficient long-context LLM inference.

entry.title: Loop, Think, & Generalize: Implicit Reasoning in Recurrent-Depth Transformers

author.name: Harsh Kohli, Srinivasan Parthasarathy, Huan Sun, Yuekun Yao

entry.summary: Studies implicit reasoning in recurrent-depth transformers that iterate over the same layers, investigating systematic generalization and depth extrapolation for compositional knowledge composition within a single forward pass.

entry.title: Dual-Pool Token-Budget Routing for Cost-Efficient and Reliable LLM Serving

author.name: Xunzhuo Liu, Bowei He, Xue Liu, Andy Luo, Haichen Zhang, Huamin Chen

entry.summary: Proposes dual-pool token-budget routing for vLLM serving that partitions GPU fleets into short-context (high-throughput) and long-context (high-capacity) pools. Addresses the practical problem that 80-95% of requests are short but served under worst-case configurations, wasting 4-8x throughput capacity.

entry.title: Guardian-as-an-Advisor: Advancing Next-Generation Guardian Models for Trustworthy LLMs

author.name: Yue Huang, Haomin Zhuang, Jiayi Ye, Han Bao, Yanbo Wang, Hang Hua, Siyuan Wu, Pin-Yu Chen, Xiangliang Zhang

entry.summary: Introduces Guardian-as-an-Advisor (GaaA), a soft-gating safety pipeline where a guardian model predicts risk labels with explanations and prepends advice to queries, keeping the base model operating under its original spec. Trained on 208k+ multi-domain GuardSet dataset.

entry.title: Symbiotic-MoE: Unlocking the Synergy between Generation and Understanding

author.name: Xiangyue Liu, Zijian Zhang, Miles Yang, Zhao Zhong, Liefeng Bo, Ping Tan

entry.summary: Proposes Symbiotic-MoE, a pre-training framework that resolves task interference between generation and understanding in multimodal LLMs using Mixture-of-Experts without parameter overhead. Addresses routing collapse where generative gradients dominate expert utilization.

entry.title: What Drives Representation Steering? A Mechanistic Case Study on Steering Refusal

author.name: Stephen Cheng, Sarah Wiegreffe, Dinesh Manocha

entry.summary: Investigates causal mechanisms underlying steering vectors in LLMs through a refusal case study. Discovers different steering methods leverage functionally interchangeable circuits, primarily interacting through OV attention circuits.

entry.title: Ads in AI Chatbots? An Analysis of How Large Language Models Navigate Conflicts of Interest

author.name: Addison J. Wu, Ryan Liu, Shuyue Stella Li, Yulia Tsvetkov, Thomas L. Griffiths

entry.summary: Provides a framework for categorizing how advertising conflicts of interest might lead LLMs to change recommendations. Studies what LLMs do (and should do) when sponsored products conflict with optimal user advice.

entry.title: Seeing but Not Thinking: Routing Distraction in Multimodal Mixture-of-Experts

author.name: Haolei Xu, Haiwen Hong, Hongxing Li, Rui Zhou, Yang Zhang, Longtao Huang, Hui Xue, Yongliang Shen, Weiming Lu, Yueting Zhuang

entry.summary: Identifies 'Seeing but Not Thinking' in multimodal MoE models where models accurately perceive images but fail at reasoning. Reveals visual experts and domain experts are layer-wise separated, with image inputs causing routing divergence in middle layers.

entry.title: GameWorld: Towards Standardized and Verifiable Evaluation of Multimodal Game Agents

author.name: Mingyu Ouyang, Siyuan Hu, Kevin Qinghong Lin, Hwee Tou Ng, Mike Zheng Shou

entry.summary: Presents GameWorld, a benchmark for evaluating multimodal LLM agents as game players in browser environments, with standardized action interfaces and verifiable evaluation. Studies both computer-use agents and API-based agents.

entry.title: SciFigDetect: A Benchmark for AI-Generated Scientific Figure Detection

author.name: You Hu, Chenzhuo Zhao, Changfa Mo, Haotian Liu, Xiaobai Li

entry.summary: Presents SciFigDetect, the first benchmark for detecting AI-generated scientific figures, using an agent-based pipeline to generate realistic synthetic figures from licensed papers. Addresses a growing research integrity concern.

entry.title: Steering the Verifiability of Multimodal AI Hallucinations

author.name: Jianhong Pang, Ruoxi Cheng, Ziyi Ye, Xingjun Ma, Zuxuan Wu, Xuanjing Huang, Yu-Gang Jiang

entry.summary: Studies the verifiability of multimodal AI hallucinations, constructing a dataset from 4,470 human responses to categorize hallucinations by how easily humans can detect them. Proposes methods to steer hallucination verifiability for different security/usability demands.

entry.title: Visual prompting reimagined: The power of the Activation Prompts

author.name: Yihua Zhang, Hongkang Li, Yuguang Yao, Aochuan Chen, Shuai Zhang, Pin-Yu Chen, Meng Wang, Sijia Liu

entry.summary: Introduces Activation Prompts (AP), extending visual prompting from input-level to activation-level universal perturbations for adapting pretrained vision models. Reduces the performance gap between visual prompting and conventional fine-tuning.

entry.title: FlowGuard: Towards Lightweight In-Generation Safety Detection for Diffusion Models via Linear Latent Decoding

author.name: Jinghan Yang, Yihe Fan, Xudong Pan, Min Yang

entry.summary: Introduces FlowGuard, a cross-model in-generation NSFW detection framework for diffusion models that inspects intermediate denoising steps using linear approximation of latent decoding.

entry.title: Reason in Chains, Learn in Trees: Self-Rectification and Grafting for Multi-turn Agent Policy Optimization

author.name: Yu Li, Sizhe Tang, Tian Lan

entry.summary: Proposes T-STAR, a framework that consolidates sampled RL trajectories into a unified 'Cognitive Tree' to identify critical steps and enable better credit assignment in multi-turn agent tasks, addressing sparse reward challenges.

entry.title: Blending Human and LLM Expertise to Detect Hallucinations and Omissions in Mental Health Chatbot Responses

author.name: Khizar Hussain, Bradley A. Malin, Zhijun Yin, Susannah Leigh Rose, Murat Kantarcioglu

entry.summary: Shows that LLM-as-judge methods achieve only 52% accuracy on mental health counseling data for hallucination detection, and proposes a framework integrating human expertise with LLMs for domain-informed feature extraction.

entry.title: $S^3$: Stratified Scaling Search for Test-Time in Diffusion Language Models

author.name: Ahsan Bilal, Muhammad Ahmed Mohsin, Muhammad Umer, Asad Aali, Muhammad Usman Khanzada, Muhammad Usman Rafique, Zihao He, Emily Fox, Dean F. Hougen

entry.summary: Proposes S³ (Stratified Scaling Search), a verifier-guided search method for diffusion language models that reallocates compute during the denoising process rather than at the final output stage. Addresses limitations of naive best-of-K sampling for test-time scaling of DLMs.

entry.title: WebSP-Eval: Evaluating Web Agents on Website Security and Privacy Tasks

author.name: Guruprasad Viswanathan Ramesh, Asmit Nayak, Basieem Siddique, Kassem Fawaz

entry.summary: Introduces WebSP-Eval, a benchmark of 200 tasks across 28 websites for evaluating web agents on security and privacy tasks like managing cookies, configuring privacy settings, and revoking sessions.

entry.title: Toward a universal foundation model for graph-structured data

author.name: Sakib Mostafa, Lei Xing, Md. Tauhidul Islam

entry.summary: Proposes a universal foundation model for graph-structured data in biomedical research, aiming to transfer across molecular networks, gene regulatory circuits, and knowledge graphs across institutions.

entry.title: Multi-objective Evolutionary Merging Enables Efficient Reasoning Models

author.name: Mario Iacobelli, Adrian Robert Minut, Tommaso Mencattini, Donato Crisostomi, Andrea Santilli, Iacopo Masi, Emanuele Rodol\`a

entry.summary: Introduces Evo-L2S, using evolutionary model merging to formulate Long-to-Short reasoning as multi-objective optimization, explicitly trading off accuracy vs output length to create efficient reasoning models.

entry.title: Discrete Flow Matching Policy Optimization

author.name: Maojiang Su, Po-Chung Hsieh, Weimin Wu, Mingcheng Lu, Jiunhau Chen, Jerry Yao-Chieh Hu, Han Liu

entry.summary: Introduces DoMinO, a framework for RL fine-tuning of Discrete Flow Matching models by viewing DFM sampling as a multi-step MDP. Provides clean policy gradient formulation with total-variation regularizers.

entry.title: Efficient Quantization of Mixture-of-Experts with Theoretical Generalization Guarantees

author.name: Mohammed Nowaz Rabbani Chowdhury, Kaoutar El Maghraoui, Hsinyu Tsai, Naigang Wang, Geoffrey W. Burr, Liu Liu, Meng Wang

entry.summary: Proposes a theoretically grounded expert-wise mixed-precision quantization strategy for Mixture-of-Experts models that assigns bit-widths based on expert sensitivity, with generalization guarantees.

entry.title: SHAPE: Stage-aware Hierarchical Advantage via Potential Estimation for LLM Reasoning

author.name: Zhengyang Ai, Zikang Shan, Xiaodong Ai, Jingxian Tang, Hangkai Hu, Pinyan Lu

entry.summary: Proposes SHAPE, a framework for process supervision in LLM reasoning that uses stage-aware hierarchical advantage estimation at segment and token levels, prioritizing breakthroughs in low-potential states.

entry.title: MoBiE: Efficient Inference of Mixture of Binary Experts under Post-Training Quantization

author.name: Zhixiong Zhao, Zukang Xu, Zhixuan Chen, Dawei Yang

entry.summary: Proposes MoBiE, the first binarization framework specifically designed for Mixture-of-Experts LLMs, addressing cross-expert redundancy, task-agnostic importance estimation, and routing shifts caused by quantization.

entry.title: SkillTrojan: Backdoor Attacks on Skill-Based Agent Systems

author.name: Yunhao Feng, Yifan Ding, Yingshui Tan, Boren Zheng, Yanming Guo, Xiaolong Li, Kun Zhai, Yishan Li, Wenke Huang

entry.summary: Introduces SkillTrojan, a backdoor attack targeting skill-based agent systems by embedding malicious logic in skill implementations rather than model parameters, distributing encrypted payloads across multiple benign-looking skills.

entry.title: MICA: Multivariate Infini Compressive Attention for Time Series Forecasting

author.name: Willa Potosnak, Nina \.Zukowska, Micha{\l} Wili\'nski, Dan Howarth, Ignacy St\k{e}pka, Mononito Goswami, Artur Dubrawski

entry.summary: Proposes MICA, an architecture extending channel-independent Transformers to channel-dependent forecasting by adapting efficient attention techniques to the channel dimension. Achieves linear scaling with channel count and context length, addressing the quadratic scaling problem of full cross-channel attention.

entry.title: Towards Accurate and Calibrated Classification: Regularizing Cross-Entropy From A Generative Perspective

author.name: Qipeng Zhan, Zhuoping Zhou, Li Shen

entry.summary: Proposes Generative Cross-Entropy (GCE) loss that maximizes p(x|y) and is equivalent to cross-entropy with a class-level confidence regularizer. Addresses the accuracy-calibration trade-off in deep neural networks, achieving improvements across CIFAR-10/100, Tiny-ImageNet, and medical imaging.

entry.title: Geometric Properties of the Voronoi Tessellation in Latent Semantic Manifolds of Large Language Models

author.name: Marshall Brett

entry.summary: Empirically studies Voronoi tessellation properties in LLM representation spaces using Qwen3.5-4B-Base, validating a linear scaling law for expressibility gap (R²=0.9997) and discovering a mid-layer geometric ambiguity regime. Shows the tessellation is reshapable, suggesting connections to model editing.

entry.title: STQuant: Spatio-Temporal Adaptive Framework for Optimizer Quantization in Large Multimodal Model Training

author.name: Minglu Liu, Cunchen Hu, Liangliang Xu, Fengming Tang, Ruijia Wang, Fu Yu

entry.summary: Proposes STQuant, a framework for dynamic precision allocation of optimizer states during large multimodal model training, varying precision across layers, state variables, and training steps. Reduces memory footprint while maintaining model quality through adaptive quantization.

entry.title: Are Stochastic Multi-objective Bandits Harder than Single-objective Bandits?

author.name: Changkun Guan, Mengfan Xu

entry.summary: Studies whether stochastic multi-objective bandits are fundamentally harder than single-objective bandits. Shows that contrary to existing work suggesting dimensionality-dependent Pareto regret, the answer may be negative, resolving a tension between adversarial and stochastic settings.

entry.title: Revisiting Fairness Impossibility with Endogenous Behavior

author.name: Elizabeth Maggie Penn, John W. Patty

entry.summary: Revisits algorithmic fairness impossibility results by incorporating endogenous behavior: when people adjust actions in anticipation of classification, the 'stakes' of classification shape outcomes. Shows fairness impossibility results may not hold when behavioral responses are accounted for.

entry.title: Stochastic Auto-conditioned Fast Gradient Methods with Optimal Rates

author.name: Yao Ji, Guanghui Lan

entry.summary: Proposes stochastic auto-conditioned fast gradient methods achieving optimal rates for composite convex optimization without prior knowledge of problem parameters. Extends parameter-free acceleration to the stochastic setting, resolving a technically challenging open problem.

entry.title: NestPipe: Large-Scale Recommendation Training on 1,500+ Accelerators via Nested Pipelining

author.name: Zhida Jiang, Zhaolong Xing, Huichao Chai, Tianxing Sun, Qiang Peng, Baopeng Yuan, Jiaxing Wang, Hua Du, Zhixin Wu, Xuemiao Li, Yikui Cao, Xinyu Liu, Yongxiang Feng, Zhen Chen, Ke Zhang

entry.summary: NestPipe is a large-scale decentralized embedding training framework for trillion-parameter recommendation models on 1,500+ accelerators, using nested pipelining with dual-buffer and shuffle-exchange strategies to overlap communication with computation.

entry.title: Decompose, Look, and Reason: Reinforced Latent Reasoning for VLMs

author.name: Mengdan Zhu, Senhao Cheng, Liang Zhao

entry.summary: DLR proposes a reinforced latent reasoning framework for VLMs that decomposes queries into textual premises, extracts premise-conditioned continuous visual latents, and uses a novel Spherical Gaussian Latent Policy for exploration.

entry.title: DIVERSED: Relaxed Speculative Decoding via Dynamic Ensemble Verification

author.name: Ziyi Wang, Siva Rajesh Kasa, Ankith M S, Santhosh Kumar Kasa, Jiaru Zou, Sumit Negi, Ruqi Zhang, Nan Jiang, Qifan Song

entry.summary: DIVERSED relaxes speculative decoding verification by learning an ensemble-based verifier that blends draft and target model distributions with task-dependent weights, improving acceptance rates while preserving generation quality.

entry.title: Rethinking Data Mixing from the Perspective of Large Language Models

author.name: Yuanjian Xu, Tianze Sun, Changwei Xu, XinLong Zhao, Jianing Hao, Ran Chen, Yang Liu, Ruijie Xu, Stephen Chen, Guang Zhang

entry.summary: Investigates fundamental questions about data mixing in LLM training—what constitutes a domain, human-model domain alignment, and how weighting influences generalization—proposing DoGraph, a graph-constrained optimization framework for data scheduling.

entry.title: A Decomposition Perspective to Long-context Reasoning for LLMs

author.name: Yanling Xiao, Huaibing Xie, Guoliang Zhao, Shihan Dou, Shaolei Wang, Yiting Liu, Nantao Zheng, Cheng Zhang, Pluto Zhou, Zhisong Zhang, Lemao Liu

entry.summary: Decomposes long-context reasoning into atomic skills, synthesizes targeted pseudo datasets for each skill, and uses reinforcement learning on these datasets to improve LLM long-context reasoning performance.

entry.title: Guaranteeing Knowledge Integration with Joint Decoding for Retrieval-Augmented Generation

author.name: Zhengyi Zhao, Shubo Zhang, Zezhong Wang, Yuxi Zhang, Huimin Wang, Yutian Zhao, Yefeng Zheng, Binyang Li, Kam-Fai Wong, Xian Wu

entry.summary: Introduces GuarantRAG, a framework that decouples reasoning from evidence integration in RAG by first generating an answer from parametric knowledge alone, then guaranteeing integration of retrieved evidence. Addresses the known 'integration bottleneck' where LLMs fail to use retrieved documents due to conflicts with internal knowledge.

entry.title: Initialisation Determines the Basin: Efficient Codebook Optimisation for Extreme LLM Quantization

author.name: Ian W. Kennedy, Nafise Sadat Moosavi

entry.summary: Shows that codebook initialization is the dominant bottleneck for extreme (2-bit) LLM quantization using additive quantization. Proposes OA-EM, an output-aware EM initialization method using Hessian-weighted Mahalanobis distance, improving 2-bit quantization quality.

entry.title: When to Trust Tools? Adaptive Tool Trust Calibration For Tool-Integrated Math Reasoning

author.name: Ruotao Xu, Yixin Ji, Yu Luo, Jinpeng Li, Dong Li, Peifeng Li, Juntao Li, Min Zhang

entry.summary: Investigates when LLMs with tool-integrated reasoning should trust tool outputs vs. their own reasoning. Finds models tend to believe their own reasoning over conflicting tool results, and proposes adaptive tool trust calibration.

entry.title: AI generates well-liked but templatic empathic responses

author.name: Emma Gueorguieva, Hongli Zhan, Jina Suh, Javier Hernandez, Tatiana Lau, Junyi Jessy Li, Desmond C. Ong

entry.summary: Shows that LLM empathic responses are highly formulaic, deploying a consistent template of empathy tactics (validation, paraphrasing, etc.). Develops a 10-tactic taxonomy and finds AI responses are well-liked but templatic across 3,265 AI-generated and 1,290 human responses.

entry.title: Demystifying OPD: Length Inflation and Stabilization Strategies for Large Language Models

author.name: Feng Luo, Yu-Neng Chuang, Guanchu Wang, Zicheng Xu, Xiaotian Han, Tianyi Zhang, Vladimir Braverman

entry.summary: Identifies a failure mode in on-policy distillation (OPD) where training causes abrupt length inflation and truncation collapse, leading to biased gradients and instability. Proposes StableOPD to address the interaction between student-induced data collection and distillation objectives.

entry.title: Flux Attention: Context-Aware Hybrid Attention for Efficient LLMs Inference

author.name: Quantong Qiu, Zhiyi Hong, Yi Yang, Haitian Wang, Kebin Liu, Qingqing Dang, Juntao Li, Min Zhang

entry.summary: Introduces Flux Attention, a context-aware hybrid attention framework that dynamically allocates full vs. sparse attention at the layer level rather than head level. Avoids computational load imbalance issues of head-level dynamic sparsity during autoregressive decoding.

entry.title: From Ground Truth to Measurement: A Statistical Framework for Human Labeling

author.name: Robert Chew, Stephanie Eckman, Christoph Kern, Frauke Kreuter

entry.summary: Reframes human labeling as a measurement process, decomposing annotation outcomes into instance difficulty, annotator bias, situational noise, and relational alignment. Extends classical measurement-error models for ML annotation settings.

entry.title: Optimal Decay Spectra for Linear Recurrences

author.name: Yang Cao

entry.summary: Analyzes the decay spectrum in linear recurrent models and proposes Position-Adaptive Spectral Tapering (PoST), combining spectral reparameterization with position-adaptive scaling. Proves minimax optimality for long-range memory retention.

entry.title: The Art of (Mis)alignment: How Fine-Tuning Methods Effectively Misalign and Realign LLMs in Post-Training

author.name: Rui Zhang, Hongwei Li, Yun Shen, Xinyue Shen, Wenbo Jiang, Guowen Xu, Yang Liu, Michael Backes, Yang Zhang

entry.summary: Systematically studies fine-tuning methods for both misalignment and realignment of LLMs, evaluating 4 SFT and 2 PFT methods across 4 models. Explores the interplay between adversarial misalignment and defensive realignment.

entry.title: Small Vision-Language Models are Smart Compressors for Long Video Understanding

author.name: Junjie Fei, Jun Chen, Zechun Liu, Yunyang Xiong, Chong Zhou, Wei Wen, Junlin Han, Mingchen Zhuge, Saksham Suri, Qi Qian, Shuming Liu, Lemeng Wu, Raghuraman Krishnamoorthi, Vikas Chandra, Mohamed Elhoseiny, Chenchen Zhu

entry.summary: Proposes Tempo, a framework using small VLMs as query-aware temporal compressors for long video understanding. Casts token reduction as early cross-modal distillation to generate compact, intent-aligned representations.

entry.title: Don't Overthink It: Inter-Rollout Action Agreement as a Free Adaptive-Compute Signal for LLM Agents

author.name: Khushal Sethi

entry.summary: Proposes TrACE, a training-free adaptive compute controller for LLM agents that measures inter-rollout action agreement to decide when to commit vs. sample more. High agreement means easy decision (commit early), low agreement triggers more computation.

entry.title: Entropy-Gradient Grounding: Training-Free Evidence Retrieval in Vision-Language Models

author.name: Marcel Gr\"opl, Jaewoo Jung, Seungryong Kim, Marc Pollefeys, Sunghwan Hong

entry.summary: Proposes entropy-gradient grounding for vision-language models: backpropagates entropy of next-token distribution to visual tokens to create relevance maps without training or auxiliary detectors. Identifies where to look to resolve visual ambiguity.

entry.title: OpenVLThinkerV2: A Generalist Multimodal Reasoning Model for Multi-domain Visual Tasks

author.name: Wenbo Hu, Xin Chen, Yan Gao-Tian, Yihe Deng, Nanyun Peng, Kai-Wei Chang

entry.summary: Introduces G²RPO (Gaussian GRPO), a novel RL training objective for multimodal models that replaces linear scaling with non-linear distributional matching. Addresses extreme variance in reward topologies across diverse visual tasks.

entry.title: VSAS-BENCH: Real-Time Evaluation of Visual Streaming Assistant Models

author.name: Pavan Kumar Anasosalu Vasu, Cem Koc, Fartash Faghri, Chun-Liang Li, Bo Feng, Zhengfeng Lai, Meng Cao, Oncel Tuzel, Hadi Pouransari

entry.summary: Introduces VSAS-Bench, a benchmark for evaluating streaming vision-language models on real-time visual assistance, measuring proactiveness and consistency beyond standard video understanding metrics.

entry.title: LPM 1.0: Video-based Character Performance Model

author.name: Ailing Zeng (R), Casper Yang (R), Chauncey Ge (R), Eddie Zhang (R), Garvey Xu (R), Gavin Lin (R), Gilbert Gu (R), Jeremy Pi (R), Leo Li (R), Mingyi Shi (R), Sheng Bi (R), Steven Tang (R), Thorn Hang (R), Tobey Guo (R), Vincent Li (R), Xin Tong (R), Yikang Li (R), Yuchen Sun (R), Yue (R), Zhao, Yuhan Lu, Yuwei Li, Zane Zhang, Zeshi Yang, Zi Ye

entry.summary: Presents LPM 1.0, a Large Performance Model for video-based character performance including speaking, listening, reacting, and emoting in full-duplex audio-visual conversation, addressing the expressiveness/speed/stability trilemma.

entry.title: Lighting-grounded Video Generation with Renderer-based Agent Reasoning

author.name: Ziqi Cai, Taoyu Yang, Zheng Chang, Si Li, Han Jiang, Shuchen Weng, Boxin Shi

entry.summary: Presents LiVER, a diffusion-based framework for scene-controllable video generation that conditions on explicit 3D properties (layout, lighting, camera) using renderer-based agent reasoning and a new large-scale annotated dataset.

entry.title: Uni-ViGU: Towards Unified Video Generation and Understanding via A Diffusion-Based Video Generator

author.name: Luozheng Qin, Jia Gong, Qian Qiao, Tianjiao Li, Li Xu, Haoyu Pan, Chao Qu, Zhiyu Tan, Hao Li

entry.summary: Proposes Uni-ViGU, a unified framework for video generation and understanding that extends a video generator (rather than an MLLM) as the foundation, using unified flow matching for video and text.

entry.title: MedVR: Annotation-Free Medical Visual Reasoning via Agentic Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Zheng Jiang, Heng Guo, Chengyu Fang, Changchen Xiao, Xinyang Hu, Lifeng Sun, Minfeng Xu

entry.summary: Introduces MedVR, an RL framework for annotation-free visual reasoning in medical VLMs, using entropy-guided visual regrounding and consensus-based credit assignment to reduce visual hallucination without requiring manual annotations.

entry.title: Lost in the Hype: Revealing and Dissecting the Performance Degradation of Medical Multimodal Large Language Models in Image Classification

author.name: Xun Zhu, Fanbin Mo, Xi Chen, Kaili Zheng, Shaoshuai Yang, Yiming Shi, Jian Gao, Miao Li, Ji Wu

entry.summary: Reveals that medical MLLMs consistently underperform traditional deep learning models on image classification despite massive pretraining advantages, systematically analyzing 14 open-source medical MLLMs to identify where degradation originates.

entry.title: Novel View Synthesis as Video Completion

author.name: Qi Wu, Khiem Vuong, Minsik Jeon, Srinivasa Narasimhan, Deva Ramanan

entry.summary: Formulates sparse novel view synthesis as a video completion task, leveraging the implicit multi-view knowledge in video diffusion models. Key insight: video models contain multi-view knowledge and should be order-invariant for sparse inputs.

entry.title: Visually-grounded Humanoid Agents

author.name: Hang Ye, Xiaoxuan Ma, Fan Lu, Wayne Wu, Kwan-Yee Lin, Yizhou Wang

entry.summary: Introduces Visually-grounded Humanoid Agents, a two-layer world-agent paradigm where digital humans perceive, reason, and behave using only visual observations in novel 3D environments, enabling scalable population of virtual worlds.

entry.title: Act Wisely: Cultivating Meta-Cognitive Tool Use in Agentic Multimodal Models

author.name: Shilin Yan, Jintao Tong, Hongwei Xue, Xiaojun Tang, Yangyang Wang, Kunyu Shi, Guannan Zhang, Ruixuan Li, Yixiong Zou

entry.summary: Proposes a meta-cognitive approach for agentic multimodal models that teaches them when to use external tools vs. internal knowledge, using decoupled reward optimization to avoid blind tool invocation.

entry.title: The Weaponization of Computer Vision: Tracing Military-Surveillance Ties through Conference Sponsorship

author.name: Noa Garcia, Amelia Katirai

entry.summary: Studies the weaponization of computer vision by analyzing military-surveillance company sponsorship at major CV conferences, revealing systematic ties between the field and military/surveillance applications.

entry.title: SIM1: Physics-Aligned Simulator as Zero-Shot Data Scaler in Deformable Worlds

author.name: Yunsong Zhou, Hangxu Liu, Xuekun Jiang, Xing Shen, Yuanzhen Zhou, Hui Wang, Baole Fang, Yang Tian, Mulin Yu, Qiaojun Yu, Li Ma, Hengjie Li, Hanqing Wang, Jia Zeng, Jiangmiao Pang

entry.summary: Introduces SIM1, a physics-aligned simulation engine for deformable object manipulation that grounds simulation in real-world physics, enabling zero-shot sim-to-real transfer for cloth manipulation.

entry.title: Selective Neuron Amplification for Training-Free Task Enhancement

author.name: Ryyan Akhtar

entry.summary: Explores Selective Neuron Amplification (SNA), a training-free method that increases task-relevant neuron influence at inference time without parameter changes. Finds it helps mainly when the model is uncertain, suggesting some failures are due to weak activation rather than missing capability.

entry.title: SAT: Balancing Reasoning Accuracy and Efficiency with Stepwise Adaptive Thinking

author.name: Weiyang Huang, Xuefeng Bai, Kehai Chen, Xinyang Chen, Yibin Chen, Weili Guan, Min Zhang

entry.summary: Introduces SAT (Stepwise Adaptive Thinking), framing LLM reasoning as a finite-state machine with thinking modes (Slow/Normal/Fast/Skip). Uses a lightweight process reward model for step-level difficulty-aware pruning of reasoning chains.

entry.title: LINE: LLM-based Iterative Neuron Explanations for Vision Models

author.name: Vladimir Zaigrajew, Micha{\l} Piechota, Gaspar Sekula, Przemys{\l}aw Biecek

entry.summary: Introduces LINE, a training-free iterative approach for open-vocabulary neuron labeling in vision models, using an LLM and text-to-image generator in a closed-loop to discover concepts encoded by individual neurons.

entry.title: LAMP: Lift Image-Editing as General 3D Priors for Open-world Manipulation

author.name: Jingjing Wang, Zhengdong Hong, Chong Bao, Yuke Zhu, Junhan Sun, Guofeng Zhang

entry.summary: Proposes LAMP, which lifts 2D image-editing priors into 3D for open-world robotic manipulation, using image editing models to provide fine-grained spatial reasoning that LLMs/VLMs lack.

entry.title: Weakly Supervised Distillation of Hallucination Signals into Transformer Representations

author.name: Shoaib Sadiq Salehmohamed, Jinal Prashant Thakkar, Hansika Aredla, Shaik Mohammed Omar, Shalmali Ayachit

entry.summary: Proposes a weak supervision framework to distill hallucination detection signals into a model's internal representations, combining substring matching, embedding similarity, and LLM-as-judge labels. Trains probes on transformer activations to detect hallucinations without external verification at inference time.

entry.title: Benchmarking LLM Tool-Use in the Wild

author.name: Peijie Yu, Wei Liu, Yifan Yang, Jinjian Li, Zelong Zhang, Xiao Feng, Feng Zhang
